conflicts.situation: Home is in away mode (R2 started recording on the hallway camera) and the clock reaches 23:00.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 turns off the hallway smart plug, which cuts power to the hallway camera. Recording stops while nobody is home.
conflicts.explanation: The hallway camera gets its power through plug_hall. R1 switches that plug off at 23:00, which silently cancels the recording R2 needs, and the text of R1 gives no sign of this.

conflicts.situation: At night (22:00–06:00) the home is in or switches to night mode, and motion is detected in the hallway.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R3 locks the front door for the night, then R4 unlocks it whenever someone moves in the hallway. The door can stay unlocked overnight, or flip between locked and unlocked depending on which rule fired last.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules set lock_front.lock to opposite values (locked vs. unlocked), and their triggers overlap in the same night-time window.

conflicts.situation: At 18:00 while home_mode == away
conflicts.undesired_outcome: heater_living receives both on (R1) and off (R5) at the same moment; final state is nondeterministic and the heater may run while nobody is home
conflicts.explanation: Both rules share the same time trigger and R1 has no condition excluding away mode, so they issue contradictory commands to heater_living.power.

conflicts.situation: Living room temperature exceeds 26 C, R2 opens the window and turns on the fan; cold outdoor air in heating season drops temp_living below 19 C
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R4 turns the heater on while the window remains open and fan runs, wasting energy and causing temperature oscillation
conflicts.explanation: R2's open window decreases temp_living, which triggers R4; nothing closes the window, so the heater fights the open window.

conflicts.situation: Weekday at 10:00, robot vacuum starts cleaning in the living room, typically while occupants are out.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Entrance door is unlocked although nobody is home, leaving the house open to intruders.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets the vacuum to cleaning; the moving vacuum is detected by the living-room PIR (motion_living = true), which triggers R2 to unlock the entrance door as if a person were present.

conflicts.situation: Weekday at 10:00 with home_mode == away, robot vacuum starts cleaning in the living room.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: False alarm: the indoor siren sounds with no intruder present.
conflicts.explanation: The cleaning vacuum triggers the living-room motion sensor, and R3 interprets this motion in away mode as an intrusion and activates the siren.

conflicts.situation: Kitchen smoke is detected and still present (or just handled) when the clock reaches 08:00.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R4 turns the air handler back on after R1 turned it off, spreading smoke through the apartment.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets hvac.power off for smoke safety, while R4 unconditionally sets hvac.power on at 08:00, with no check for smoke.

conflicts.situation: Smoke is detected in the kitchen while the home is switching to or already in away mode (e.g. an oven left on when residents leave).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The door is either locked during an evacuation (R2 after R1) or left unlocked while nobody is home (R1 after R2).
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets lock_door to unlocked and R2 sets it to locked. Both can fire close together, so the final state depends on which rule runs last.

conflicts.situation: The oven is on, so R3 turns on the range hood, while smoke is building up in the kitchen.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The hood clears the smoke reading, so R1 may not fire or may fire late. The door is not unlocked for evacuation and the air handler keeps running during a real fire.
conflicts.explanation: The hood (turned on by R3) sets smoke_kitchen to false, which is the trigger of R1. This can stop the smoke-safety rule from firing.

conflicts.situation: At 00:30 while the home is in night mode, and the garden camera has cloud upload and recording turned on by R2
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 turns off the office plug, which also cuts power to the router. The garden camera then loses Wi-Fi and cannot upload to the cloud, so night-time security footage is not stored off-site.
conflicts.explanation: The router is plugged into the office smart plug. Turning off the plug for standby power saving also takes the router offline, which undoes the cloud upload that R2 turned on.

conflicts.situation: At 00:30 while the home is in away mode and R3 has turned on doorbell notifications
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Turning off the office plug also turns off the router, so the doorbell can't send notifications while nobody is home.
conflicts.explanation: Doorbell notifications are sent over Wi-Fi through the router. The router is powered by the office plug, so R1 indirectly turns off what R3 is meant to keep on.

conflicts.situation: Home switches to night mode (R1 cuts strip_living), then aquarium water_temp drops below 24 C during the night.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 commands the aquarium heater on, but the heater has no power because it is plugged into the switched-off power strip; the water keeps cooling. The aquarium pump (filter/oxygen) on the same strip is also off all night, endangering the fish.
conflicts.explanation: R1 turns off strip_living, which physically powers aquarium_heater and aquarium_pump. R2 relies on the heater to keep the water warm, so its action has no effect.

conflicts.situation: Night mode is active (R5 turned the heater off) and water_temp falls below 24 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R5 keeps the heater off for quiet while R2 turns it back on. Either the night-quiet goal is violated or the water gets too cold, depending on which rule fires last.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules set aquarium_heater.power to opposite values, and both can apply at the same time at night.

conflicts.situation: Home is in away mode (R1 has closed the main water valve) and the clock reaches 06:00, so R2 starts the irrigation.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The irrigation controller shows watering as on, but no water flows. The garden stays dry for the whole time the home is away. Because soil moisture never goes above 60 %, R4 never stops the watering, so the controller stays on with nothing coming out.
conflicts.explanation: The irrigation line gets its water through the main valve, and this link isn't stated in either rule. When R1 closes valve_main, irrigation.flow is forced off, which cancels R2's flow and watering commands.

conflicts.situation: A leak in the utility room has been detected (R3 has closed the main water valve), and at 06:00 R2 starts the scheduled watering.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The scheduled irrigation can't run because there is no water, yet the controller shows watering as on. The garden goes unwatered and R4 is never triggered to stop it.
conflicts.explanation: The main valve physically supplies the irrigation line. When R3 closes it for leak protection, the flow R2 needs is cut off, and neither rule takes this into account.

conflicts.situation: Bright daytime sun pushes living-room illuminance above 800 lux, so R1 closes the blinds.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: With the daylight blocked, illuminance can drop below 150 lux. R2 then turns on the ceiling lights in the middle of a sunny day, which wastes energy and defeats the point of the glare control.
conflicts.explanation: R1's action (blinds closed) lowers lux_living, which is R2's trigger. Closing the blinds to cut glare ends up setting off artificial lighting.

conflicts.situation: At 07:30 on a bright morning, R3 opens the blinds and the sunlight lets in pushes lux_living above 800.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 closes the blinds right after the scheduled opening, so the morning 'blinds open' routine is undone and the blinds move open and then closed again.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules set blinds_living.position to opposite values (open vs. closed), and both can fire around 07:30 when daylight is strong.

conflicts.situation: From 20:00, after R1 switches on the nursery humidifier and nursery humidity rises above 55 %
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The dehumidifier switches on and fights the humidifier: wasted energy, humidity swinging around the threshold, and noise in the nursery while the baby sleeps
conflicts.explanation: The humidifier turned on by R1 raises humidity_nursery. Once it passes 55 %, R2 turns on the dehumidifier, which works against R1's goal.

conflicts.situation: At or after 20:00, when nursery humidity is above 55 % (for example because the humidifier is running)
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The dehumidifier R5 turned off for quiet sleep is turned back on by R2, so the room isn't quiet and the device may keep switching on and off
conflicts.explanation: R5 sets dehumidifier_nursery.power to off at 20:00 and R2 sets it to on whenever humidity is above 55 %. These are opposite commands to the same device at overlapping times.

conflicts.situation: The home switched to night mode the evening before, so R1 turned off the bedroom wall-switch relay. In the morning the wake-up alarm rings (alarm_clock == true) while the relay is still off.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 tries to fade the bedroom bulb in to 60 %, but the bulb gets no power. The wake-up light stays dark and the command fails or the bulb is unreachable.
conflicts.explanation: The bedroom bulb is wired behind the bedroom wall-switch relay, so switch_bedroom.power = off cuts power to bulb_bedroom. Nothing turns the relay back on before R2 runs, so R2's action cannot take effect.

conflicts.situation: Someone arrives home at about 18:00, inside R2's 17:00-19:00 window, when R1's 18:00 schedule also fires.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The thermostat is set to heat at 23 C and to eco at 19 C at the same time. The result depends on which rule runs last.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules set thermostat.mode and thermostat.setpoint to incompatible values, and both can fire at the same moment.

conflicts.situation: Someone arrives home between 17:00 and 19:00 while temp_living is below 20 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R4 sets the thermostat to heat while R2 sets it to eco. If eco wins, the room stays cold for the people who just arrived.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules write thermostat.mode with opposite values in overlapping situations. R4 does not fire again unless the temperature newly drops below 20 C.

conflicts.situation: At 08:00 the living room is below 20 C and R4 has set the thermostat to heat.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R5 switches the thermostat to eco and the cold room stays underheated. R4 does not fire again to restore heat.
conflicts.explanation: R4 and R5 write opposite values to thermostat.mode. Because R4 only fires when the temperature crosses below 20 C, R5's override stays in place.

conflicts.situation: R4 switches heating on when the room is below 20 C. With no setpoint limit and no rule turning it off, the room warms past 24 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R3 starts the air conditioner cooling while the heater is still on. They work against each other and waste energy, and cooling below 20 C fires R4 again, so the two keep alternating.
conflicts.explanation: Heating raises temp_living, which fires R3 (cooling). Cooling lowers temp_living, which fires R4 (heat). Neither rule turns the other device off.

conflicts.situation: Home is in away mode, so the garage breaker is off, and carbon monoxide is detected in the garage (e.g. a car engine left running).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The exhaust fan can't run because its circuit has no power, so CO builds up in the garage and can spread into the house.
conflicts.explanation: R1 cuts power to the garage circuit, and the exhaust fan is on that circuit. R2's fan-on command therefore does nothing (or the fan is switched off if it was already running).

conflicts.situation: The car is parked in the garage and charging (or arrives and starts charging), and the home switches to away mode.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: EV charging stops and the car is not charged while the occupants are away.
conflicts.explanation: The EV charger is on the garage circuit. R1 switching off the breaker forces charging off, which cancels what R4 set up.

conflicts.situation: CO is detected in the garage around the time the home switches to away mode (both triggers within a short window, or away mode set while CO is present).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The garage door is closed while CO is present, or it keeps switching between open and closed, so the garage isn't vented.
conflicts.explanation: R2 opens the garage door to clear CO, and R3 closes the same door when away mode starts. These are opposite commands to garage_door.position, and nothing in R3 checks for CO.

conflicts.situation: At 12:00 while home_mode == away: R1 dispenses cat food, the cat runs to the feeder and triggers the kitchen motion sensor (motion_kitchen = true).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 treats the cat's motion as an intruder and sounds the siren every day at noon while the owners are away (false alarm).
conflicts.explanation: The feeder causes the cat to move in the kitchen, which sets motion_kitchen to true. That is R2's trigger, and in away mode R2 fires even though no intruder is present.

conflicts.situation: Motion is detected in the kitchen while home_mode == home (for example, a resident walks in, or the cat triggers the sensor after R1 dispenses food).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R3 sets camera_kitchen.recording to on and R6 sets it to off at the same moment, so the result is unpredictable. The camera may record residents despite the privacy rule.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules fire on the same trigger, motion_kitchen == true. R3 has no mode condition, so in home mode it sends the opposite command to the same device state as R6.

conflicts.situation: Night mode is active before 23:30, so R2 has turned the CPAP on; at 23:30 R1 turns off the bedside plug.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The CPAP machine loses power while the user is asleep, which is a serious health risk. R2 does not fire again, so the CPAP stays off.
conflicts.explanation: The CPAP is plugged into the bedside smart plug. Cutting the plug to stop phone charging also cuts power to the CPAP that R2 is meant to keep running.

conflicts.situation: A fall is detected in the bathroom (R3 unlocks the entrance door), and the home switches to night mode during the emergency or right after it (R4 locks the door).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The entrance door ends up locked, and paramedics cannot get in to help the person who fell.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules set lock_entrance.lock to opposite values. Neither rule has a condition that excludes the other, so whichever runs last decides the lock state.

conflicts.situation: At 14:00 the sprinkler starts watering the lawn next to the terrace where the rain sensor is mounted.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The rain sensor reports rain falsely and the bedroom skylight is closed without any actual rain.
conflicts.explanation: The sprinkler spray wets the terrace rain sensor (sprinkler -> rain_sensor true), which triggers R4's skylight closing.

conflicts.situation: At 10:00 on a hot summer day, R2 opens the living room window and hot outdoor air raises temp_living above 27 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The AC starts cooling while the window is open, wasting energy and counteracting the intended fresh-air ventilation.
conflicts.explanation: Opening the window increases living room temperature, which triggers R1 to switch the AC to cool.

conflicts.situation: Around 10:00 when the AC is (or starts) cooling: R2 commands window_living open while R6 commands it closed when AC mode becomes cool (possibly triggered via R2 -> temp rise -> R1).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The living room window is opened and then closed shortly after, or remains open while the AC is cooling (R6 fires only on the transition), defeating either the airing or the cooling efficiency.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules set window_living.position to opposite values in overlapping situations.

conflicts.situation: Home switches to night mode before 01:00 (e.g., around 23:00), and at 01:00 the nightly backup is scheduled.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The NAS has no power when the 01:00 backup should start, so the nightly backup fails or is silently skipped.
conflicts.explanation: R2 turns off the closet power strip, and the NAS is plugged into that strip, so turning the strip off also cuts power to the NAS. When R1 starts the backup at 01:00, the NAS is off and cannot run it.

conflicts.situation: Night mode is active (closet strip off) while the closet temperature goes above 35 C, or the closet is already hot when night mode starts.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The cooling fan cannot run, or is cut off while running, so the closet overheats.
conflicts.explanation: The cooling fan is plugged into the closet strip. Turning the strip off with R2 forces the fan off, which overrides the 'fan on' command from R3 and stops it from cooling the closet.

conflicts.situation: The teenager's phone arrives home between 23:00 and 06:00.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 unlocks the front door, then R2 sees it unlocked and locks it again right away. The door flips between unlocked and locked, and the teenager may be locked out or find the door locked again while opening it.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules act on lock_front.lock with opposite values. R1's action is exactly what triggers R2 during the night window, so the door can't stay unlocked for the teenager arriving late.

conflicts.situation: Every day at 09:00, both rules fire at the same time on shades_office.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: One rule closes the office shades and the other opens them, so where they end up depends on execution order. Either screen-glare protection or daylight use fails.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules have the same trigger (time == 09:00) and set shades_office.position to opposite values (closed vs open).

conflicts.situation: Winter morning: at 09:00 R1 closes the exterior shades, which blocks solar gains, and temp_office drops below 20 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The radiator valve opens to make up for heat that the shades blocked. This wastes energy, and the two rules work against each other.
conflicts.explanation: Closing shades_office lowers temp_office, according to the AFFECTS edge. This makes R2's trigger (temp_office < 20) fire when it otherwise might not have.

conflicts.situation: From 19:30 onward, when R2 starts the white-noise speaker in the nursery and the baby monitor microphone picks it up, the nursery sound level can go above 60 dB.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The nursery lamp turns on even though the baby isn't crying. This can wake the baby and undo the sleep aid.
conflicts.explanation: White noise raises noise_nursery, the reading R1 uses to detect crying. R1 can't tell white noise from a crying baby, so it fires by mistake.

conflicts.situation: After 20:00, when the TV turns on and R3 switches on the soundbar, which shares a thin wall with the nursery.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Sound from the soundbar pushes the nursery level above 60 dB, and the nursery lamp turns on while the baby is asleep.
conflicts.explanation: Sound from the soundbar comes through the wall and raises noise_nursery. R1 reads this as crying and turns on the lamp when it shouldn't.

conflicts.situation: A frost warning is active at 22:00 (or issued before 22:00 and still in effect).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R6 turns off the greenhouse heater that R1 turned on for frost protection; plants are exposed to frost overnight.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets gh_heater.power=on on frost warning, R6 sets it off at 22:00 regardless of frost. Since R1 only fires when the warning is issued, the heater stays off.

conflicts.situation: Frost warning active at 22:00 when R3 switches off the outdoor plug.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The greenhouse heater loses power during a frost warning, defeating frost protection.
conflicts.explanation: The heater is plugged into plug_outdoor; turning the plug off physically cuts the heater's power even though R1 wants it on.

conflicts.situation: During a frost warning the heater runs and warms the greenhouse above 18 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The roof vent opens while the heater is still running, releasing heated air into freezing outside air and wasting energy, with heater and vent working against each other.
conflicts.explanation: R1's heating raises temp_gh above 18 C, which triggers R2 to open the vent; R1 has no off-threshold, so the heater keeps running against the open vent.

conflicts.situation: The home is in away mode, so R2 has started hallway camera recording, and then the clock reaches 23:00.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 switches off the hallway smart plug. That cuts power to the hallway camera and stops the security recording R2 started while nobody is home.
conflicts.explanation: The hallway camera gets its power through plug_hall. Turning the plug off (R1) also turns camera_hall off, which silently overrides R2's recording.

conflicts.situation: The home switches to night mode, which is usually between 22:00 and 06:00, and motion is detected in the hallway during that window.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The front door is unlocked at night soon after R3 locked it. Hallway motion from a resident, a pet or an intruder near the door leaves the home unsecured overnight.
conflicts.explanation: R3 sets lock_front to locked and R4 sets it to unlocked. Both can fire in the same night window, so their commands to the same lock contradict each other.

conflicts.situation: At 18:00 while home_mode == away
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Living room heater receives both on and off commands; final state depends on execution order and the heater may run in an empty house
conflicts.explanation: Both rules trigger at the same time on heater_living.power with opposite values, and R1 has no condition excluding away mode.

conflicts.situation: Heating season: living room exceeds 26 C, R2 opens the window; cold outdoor air drops temp_living below 19 C while the window stays open
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Heater turned on by R4 while the window is still open, wasting energy and possibly cycling between the two rules
conflicts.explanation: R2's open window lowers temp_living (AFFECTS edge), triggering R4; no rule closes the window, so heating and ventilation run against each other.

conflicts.situation: After 18:00 the heater turned on by R1 raises temp_living above 26 C
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Window opened and fan turned on while the heater keeps running, so heating and cooling run at the same time and waste energy
conflicts.explanation: R1's heater raises temp_living and triggers R2, but neither rule switches the heater off, so the cooling response runs against a heater that stays on.

conflicts.situation: Weekdays at 10:00, when the robot vacuum starts cleaning in the living room, most likely while nobody is home.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The entrance door gets unlocked while the house is empty, which is a security risk.
conflicts.explanation: The moving vacuum sets off the living room motion sensor (motion_living = true). R2 reads that motion as someone being home and unlocks the entrance door.

conflicts.situation: Weekdays at 10:00 while the home is in away mode and the vacuum starts cleaning.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The indoor siren goes off with no intruder present (a false alarm).
conflicts.explanation: The vacuum's movement is picked up by the living room motion sensor. Because the home is in away mode, R3 treats it as an intruder and turns on the siren.

conflicts.situation: Kitchen smoke is detected (or still present) around 08:00; R1 has turned the air handler off and the 08:00 schedule fires.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The air handler is turned back on during a smoke event, spreading smoke through the apartment.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets hvac.power off when smoke is detected while R4 sets hvac.power on at 08:00 with no smoke check, so the two rules issue opposite commands to the same device.

conflicts.situation: Smoke is detected in the kitchen while the home mode switches to away (e.g., occupants leave or the oven was left on while away).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The apartment door is re-locked (or left locked) during a fire, blocking evacuation and emergency access.
conflicts.explanation: R1 unlocks the door on smoke and R2 locks it on away mode; both can fire in the same period, and the last command wins.

conflicts.situation: The oven is on and starts producing smoke (e.g., an oven fire); R3 has turned the range hood on.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The hood clears smoke from the kitchen so the detector does not report it or reports it late. R1 then does not unlock the door for evacuation or shut off the air handler.
conflicts.explanation: The hood being on sets smoke_kitchen to false, according to the AFFECTS edge. This suppresses the trigger condition R1 depends on to start its emergency actions.

conflicts.situation: Home is in night mode (R2 has enabled garden camera cloud upload/recording) and the clock reaches 00:30, when R1 turns off the office plug.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The router loses power, so the garden camera can no longer upload recordings to the cloud during the night; R2's security intent is silently defeated.
conflicts.explanation: The router is plugged into the office smart plug; switching the plug off cuts the router, and the camera's cloud upload depends on Wi-Fi.

conflicts.situation: Home is in away mode (R3 has enabled doorbell notifications) at 00:30, when R1 turns off the office plug.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Router powers off and doorbell notifications are no longer delivered while the occupants are away.
conflicts.explanation: The office plug feeds the router; doorbell notifications are delivered over Wi-Fi, so R1 indirectly disables what R3 enabled.

conflicts.situation: Night mode is on, so R5 has turned the aquarium heater off, and the water temperature then drops below 24 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The heater flips between off and on. R2 turns it back on and undoes R5's goal of keeping the room quiet. If R5 fires while the water is already cold, the fish lose heat.
conflicts.explanation: R5 sets aquarium_heater.power to off and R2 sets it to on. Both rules can apply during night mode when the water is cold, so they give opposite commands to the same device.

conflicts.situation: Night mode is on, so R1 has switched off the living room power strip that feeds the aquarium heater and pump. The water temperature then drops below 24 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 turns the heater on, but it gets no power, so the water keeps cooling. The aquarium pump is also off, so there is no filtering or oxygen overnight, which puts the fish at risk.
conflicts.explanation: The heater and pump are plugged into strip_living. The rules don't say this, but cutting the strip's power stops R2's heater-on action from doing anything.

conflicts.situation: Home is in away mode (R1 has closed the main water valve) and at 06:00 R2 starts garden watering.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 switches the irrigation on, but no water flows because the irrigation line is supplied through the closed main valve. The garden goes unwatered while the controller still shows watering as on.
conflicts.explanation: Closing valve_main physically stops irrigation.flow. This dependency is not stated in either rule, so R2's watering command silently fails whenever the home is in away mode.

conflicts.situation: A leak in the utility room has triggered R3 and closed the main valve. Later, at 06:00, R2 starts watering.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Irrigation is commanded on but gets no water supply. The garden is not watered while the controller shows watering as on, and soil moisture never rises, so R4 never fires to end the cycle.
conflicts.explanation: The irrigation line runs through valve_main. Once R3 closes it, R2's flow and watering commands cannot take effect.

conflicts.situation: Daytime with strong sunlight: lux_living rises above 800, R1 closes the living room blinds.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Closing the blinds drops lux_living below 150, so R2 switches the ceiling lights on in broad daylight, wasting energy and counteracting the purpose of the glare control.
conflicts.explanation: R1's action (blinds closed) decreases lux_living via the 'closed blinds block daylight' effect, which unexpectedly satisfies R2's trigger lux_living < 150. The two rules then work against each other on the same illuminance variable.

conflicts.situation: From 20:00, the nursery humidifier (R1) runs and nursery humidity rises above 55 %.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 turns on the dehumidifier, so the humidifier and dehumidifier run against each other. This wastes energy, makes humidity swing up and down, and puts the loud dehumidifier on during the baby's sleep.
conflicts.explanation: The humidifier raises humidity_nursery, and that change triggers R2. R2 then works directly against R1's goal.

conflicts.situation: After 20:00, when nursery humidity goes above 55 %. R1's humidifier makes this very likely.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The dehumidifier R5 turned off for quiet sleep is turned back on by R2, so the nursery is noisy at night.
conflicts.explanation: R5 sets dehumidifier_nursery.power to off and R2 sets it to on. Both can fire during the same night, and nothing in either rule stops R2 during sleep hours.

conflicts.situation: The home switched to night mode in the evening, so R1 turned off the bedroom wall switch relay. The next morning the wake-up alarm rings and R2 tries to fade the bedroom bulb in to 60%.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The bedroom bulb has no power because the relay in front of it is off. The wake-up light stays dark and R2's on and brightness commands do nothing.
conflicts.explanation: The bedroom bulb is wired behind the bedroom wall switch relay. When R1 turns the relay off, the bulb loses power, and no rule turns the relay back on before R2 runs.

conflicts.situation: At 18:00 when someone arrives home within the 17:00-19:00 window (home_mode becomes home)
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Thermostat receives heat/23 C from R1 and eco/19 C from R2; final state depends on execution order, comfort setting unpredictable
conflicts.explanation: Both rules target thermostat.mode and setpoint with incompatible values and their trigger/condition windows overlap at 18:00.

conflicts.situation: Living room exceeds 24 C, AC starts cooling and is never switched off; temperature drops below 20 C
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Thermostat heats while the AC still cools; simultaneous heating and cooling, wasted energy and temperature oscillation
conflicts.explanation: R3's cooling lowers temp_living until R4 fires and turns heating on; heating then raises temp_living back toward R3's trigger, so the rules keep triggering each other.

conflicts.situation: Living room below 20 C while someone arrives home between 17:00 and 19:00
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R4 sets heat but R2 sets eco (19 C); if eco wins the room stays below 20 C and R4's intent is defeated
conflicts.explanation: Both rules set thermostat.mode to incompatible values (heat vs eco) in overlapping situations.

conflicts.situation: Living room drops below 20 C shortly before or around 08:00
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R4 switches the thermostat to heat, then R5 switches it to eco at 08:00; the room stays cold and R4 does not re-fire because it is edge-triggered
conflicts.explanation: Both rules target thermostat.mode with incompatible values (heat vs eco) and can fire around the same time.

conflicts.situation: Home is in away mode (garage breaker switched off by R1) and carbon monoxide is detected in the garage.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The exhaust fan R2 turns on has no power, so CO is not ventilated from the garage.
conflicts.explanation: R1 switches off the garage breaker, and the exhaust fan is on the garage circuit. The fan stays off even though R2 commands it on.

conflicts.situation: The car is parked in the garage and charging (R4) when the home switches to away mode.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: EV charging stops, so the car may not be charged when needed.
conflicts.explanation: The EV charger is on the garage circuit. R1 cuts the breaker, which overrides the charging that R4 started.

conflicts.situation: Carbon monoxide is detected in the garage around the time the home switches to away mode.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The garage door gets contradictory commands. If it closes, CO is trapped inside; if it opens, the house is left with the garage door open while the occupants are away.
conflicts.explanation: R2 sets garage_door to open and R3 sets it to closed. Their triggers can occur together.

conflicts.situation: Kitchen motion detected while home_mode == home
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Kitchen camera recording is set both on (R3) and off (R6); final state depends on execution order, violating privacy intent or leaving camera in unpredictable state
conflicts.explanation: R3 has no mode condition, so it fires together with R6 in home mode and they issue opposite commands to camera_kitchen.recording.

conflicts.situation: 12:00 while home_mode == away
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Siren sounds (false alarm) every day at noon when the occupants are away
conflicts.explanation: R1 dispenses cat food, the cat runs to the feeder and triggers motion_kitchen, which fires R2's intrusion alarm in away mode.

conflicts.situation: Home is in night mode with the CPAP running (R2), and at 23:30 R1 turns off the bedside plug.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The CPAP is plugged into the bedside plug, so it loses power while the user is asleep. A life-support medical device stops during sleep.
conflicts.explanation: R1 means to cut power to a phone charger only, but the CPAP also draws power from plug_bedside. Turning the plug off undoes what R2 is meant to guarantee, and R2 won't turn the CPAP back on because night mode doesn't fire again.

conflicts.situation: A fall is detected in the bathroom and R3 unlocks the entrance door. Then, or at about the same time, the home switches to night mode (for example on a schedule at bedtime) and R4 runs.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R4 locks the entrance door again, so paramedics can't get in to reach the person who fell.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules set lock_entrance.lock to opposite values, and their triggers can happen close together. Whichever rule runs last decides the state, so the emergency unlock can be overridden.

conflicts.situation: At 10:00 while the living room AC is already cooling (temp_living > 27), or whenever AC cooling starts after the 10:00 opening.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: window_living is commanded open by R2 and closed by R6; the window opens while the AC is cooling, so cooling energy is wasted, and the rules fight over the window state.
conflicts.explanation: R2 opens the living room window at a fixed time regardless of AC state, while R6 requires the window closed whenever the AC cools; both target window_living.position with opposite values.

conflicts.situation: Summer day: R2 opens the living room window at 10:00 and hot outdoor air raises temp_living above 27 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Opening the window for fresh air causes the AC to start cooling (and via R6, the window to close again), wasting energy and defeating the fresh-air intent.
conflicts.explanation: window_living open increases temp_living, which is the trigger of R1 (temp_living > 27), so R2's action unexpectedly fires R1.

conflicts.situation: At 14:00 the sprinkler starts watering the lawn on a dry day; its spray hits the terrace rain sensor.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The bedroom skylight closes even though it is not raining (false rain detection).
conflicts.explanation: sprinkler.watering = on sets rain_sensor to true, which is the trigger of R4, so R4 closes the skylight unexpectedly.

conflicts.situation: Night mode is turned on before 01:00 (or the backup is still running when it is turned on), so R2 switches off the closet power strip.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The NAS has no power, so the 01:00 backup from R1 cannot start, or a running backup is cut off mid-job. This can leave the backup incomplete or corrupted.
conflicts.explanation: The NAS is plugged into the closet strip. When R2 turns the strip off, the NAS loses power, which blocks what R1 is trying to do with nas.backup.

conflicts.situation: Night mode is on and the closet strip is off, while the closet is above 35 °C (for example, heat left over from a backup or a warm night).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R3 turns the cooling fan on, but the fan has no power. The closet stays too hot and the fan's reported state may not match what is really happening.
conflicts.explanation: The cooling fan is plugged into the closet strip. When R2 turns the strip off, the fan is forced off and R3 can no longer cool the closet.

conflicts.situation: The teenager's phone arrives home between 23:00 and 06:00 (for example, coming home late at night).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 unlocks the front door, and R2 locks it again right away. The door keeps switching between locked and unlocked, and the teenager may be locked out, or the door may end up in a state nobody intended.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules set lock_front.lock on the same device to opposite values. R1's unlock is exactly what triggers R2 during the night window, so the two actions cancel each other out.

conflicts.situation: Every day at 09:00, when both time triggers fire together.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The office shades are told to close and open at the same moment. Where they end up depends on which command runs last, so the shades may be wrong for screen work or for using daylight.
conflicts.explanation: R1 and R6 have the same trigger (time == 09:00) and set shades_office.position to opposite values. Neither rule has a condition that stops them from firing together.

conflicts.situation: Winter mornings after 09:00, when R1 has closed the exterior shades and the office temperature falls below 20 °C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The radiator starts heating because the shades are blocking free solar heat. This wastes energy and works against the intent of the shading rule.
conflicts.explanation: Closed shades block winter solar gains, which lowers temp_office. That indirect cooling triggers R2, so the radiator turns on to replace heat the shades are blocking.

conflicts.situation: At 19:30 R2 starts the nursery white-noise speaker; the baby monitor microphone picks it up and noise_nursery rises above 60 dB.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 thinks the baby is crying and turns on the nursery lamp when there is no crying. This can wake the baby at bedtime and makes R1 unreliable as a crying alert.
conflicts.explanation: White noise raises the measured nursery sound level (AFFECTS edge), which meets R1's trigger noise_nursery > 60.

conflicts.situation: After 20:00 the TV is turned on, so R3 turns on the soundbar; its sound carries through the thin shared wall and the nursery reading goes above 60 dB.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The nursery lamp turns on while the baby sleeps because of TV audio, not crying.
conflicts.explanation: The soundbar raises noise_nursery through the shared wall (AFFECTS edge), which falsely triggers R1.

conflicts.situation: A frost warning is active (heater turned on by R1) when the clock reaches 22:00.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R6 switches the greenhouse heater off during a frost night, so plants may freeze.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets gh_heater.power on and R6 sets it off. Both can apply on the same night. R1 is edge-triggered by the warning and will not turn the heater back on.

conflicts.situation: A frost warning is active and the heater is running (R1) at 22:00, when R3 turns off the outdoor plug.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The heater loses power and the greenhouse is unheated during frost.
conflicts.explanation: The greenhouse heater is powered through plug_outdoor. Turning the plug off cuts the heater's power, which is not stated in R3's text, and undoes R1's action.

conflicts.situation: During a frost warning, the heater (R1) warms the greenhouse above 18 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 opens the roof vent in freezing weather and releases the heat. Energy is wasted and the temperature can fall quickly.
conflicts.explanation: The heater raises temp_gh, which triggers R2 to open the vent. The vent then lowers temp_gh, so the heater and vent work against each other during frost.

conflicts.situation: Home is in away mode, so R2 has started recording on the hallway camera, and the time reaches 23:00.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 switches off the hallway smart plug, which also cuts power to the hallway camera. Recording stops while nobody is home, leaving the front door unmonitored.
conflicts.explanation: The hallway camera gets its power through plug_hall. R1 turns the plug off without checking the mode, so it defeats the recording R2 depends on.

conflicts.situation: Night mode is active (usually between 22:00 and 06:00) and motion is detected in the hallway, for example someone walking to the bathroom or the kitchen.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R3 locks the front door for the night, then R4 unlocks it as soon as there is hallway motion. The door can stay unlocked all night.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules act on lock_front.lock with opposite values (locked vs. unlocked), and both can fire in the same night-time window. Nothing stops them from undoing each other.

conflicts.situation: At 18:00 while home_mode == away
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Living room heater is commanded both on and off simultaneously; result depends on execution order and the heater may run in an empty house.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules fire on the same time trigger and set heater_living.power to opposite values; R1 has no away-mode exception, so it can override R5.

conflicts.situation: Living room exceeds 26 C (e.g. after heater ran), R2 opens the window; in heating season cold outdoor air drops temp_living below 19 C
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R4 turns the heater on while the window is open and the fan runs; heating against an open window wastes energy and temperature oscillates, with nothing closing the window or turning the heater off.
conflicts.explanation: R2's window opening decreases temp_living, which triggers R4's heater; the heater then raises temp again toward R2's threshold, so the rules feed each other.

conflicts.situation: Weekdays at 10:00, when the robot vacuum starts cleaning in the living room, possibly while nobody is home
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The entrance door is unlocked even though nobody is home, which leaves the house open to intruders.
conflicts.explanation: R1 starts the vacuum, and its movement sets motion_living to true. R2 reads that as a person being home and unlocks the entrance door.

conflicts.situation: Weekdays at 10:00 while home_mode is away and the vacuum is cleaning the living room
conflicts.undesired_outcome: False alarm: the indoor siren sounds with no intruder present.
conflicts.explanation: The vacuum started by R1 is picked up by the living room motion sensor. Because the home is in away mode, R3 treats this as an intrusion and turns on the siren.

conflicts.situation: Smoke is detected in the kitchen and R1 turns off the air handler. At 08:00, while there is still smoke, R4 turns it back on.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The air handler restarts during a smoke or fire event and spreads smoke through the apartment, cancelling R1's safety shutoff.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets hvac.power to off and R4 sets hvac.power to on. R4's fixed time trigger does not check for smoke, so the two rules can conflict on the same device.

conflicts.situation: Smoke is detected while the household mode switches to away, or the mode switches to away during or after a smoke event.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Either the door is locked during an evacuation, or it is left unlocked while the apartment is empty.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets lock_door to unlocked and R2 sets it to locked. Neither rule excludes the other's situation, so whichever fires last decides the door's state.

conflicts.situation: The oven is on, so R3 runs the range hood, and smoke starts in the kitchen (for example, an oven fire).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The hood clears the smoke so the detector stays false. R1 is delayed or never fires, so the door is not unlocked and the air handler is not shut off during a real fire.
conflicts.explanation: R3 turns the hood on, and the hood sets smoke_kitchen to false. smoke_kitchen is R1's trigger, so R3's action can stop R1 from firing.

conflicts.situation: At 00:30 while the home is in night mode and R2 has turned on cloud upload and recording on the garden camera.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The router loses power, so the garden camera can no longer upload recordings to the cloud. Night-time security footage is not stored off-site.
conflicts.explanation: The router is plugged into the office smart plug. When R1 turns that plug off, the router goes off and Wi-Fi drops, so the cloud upload that R2 turned on stops working.

conflicts.situation: At 00:30 while the home is in away mode and R3 has turned on doorbell notifications.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Doorbell notifications are no longer delivered, so the residents who are away miss visitors or security events at the entrance.
conflicts.explanation: R1 turns off the office plug, which also powers off the router. The doorbell sends notifications over Wi-Fi, so without the router the notifications that R3 turned on stop working.

conflicts.situation: Home is in night mode; R5 has switched the aquarium heater off and the water temperature falls below 24 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Heater is commanded off and on in the same night period: either fish are exposed to cold water or the quiet-night goal is broken, with the heater switching back and forth.
conflicts.explanation: R5 sets aquarium_heater.power=off on night mode, while R2 sets it on when water_temp<24, which becomes likely once the heater is off overnight.

conflicts.situation: Night mode: R1 turns off the living room power strip, then aquarium water temperature drops below 24 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2's command to turn on the heater has no effect because the heater has no power; the aquarium cools (and the filter/oxygen pump is also off).
conflicts.explanation: The aquarium heater is plugged into strip_living, so cutting the strip's power silently overrides R2's heater-on action.

conflicts.situation: The home is in away mode, so R1 has closed the main water valve, and it reaches 06:00, when R2 fires.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 sets the irrigation to flow and water, but no water reaches the sprinklers. The garden goes unwatered while the controller reports that watering is on.
conflicts.explanation: The irrigation line is fed through the main water valve. With that valve closed, irrigation.flow is forced off, which cancels R2's action. Neither rule mentions this link.

conflicts.situation: A leak in the utility room has made R3 close the main water valve, and 06:00 comes before the valve is reopened.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The scheduled garden watering fails even though R2 sets irrigation flow and watering to on, and the irrigation state no longer matches what actually happens.
conflicts.explanation: Closing the main valve cuts the water supply to the irrigation line, so R2's watering command cannot work. Neither rule mentions this link.

conflicts.situation: Sunny daytime: lux_living goes above 800, so R1 closes the living room blinds.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Closing the blinds cuts off daylight and lux_living drops below 150. R2 then turns on the ceiling lights in the middle of a sunny day. This wastes energy and undoes the point of using daylight. If the lights push lux back up, the two rules can keep triggering each other.
conflicts.explanation: R1's action (blinds closed) lowers lux_living, which is R2's trigger. R1 and R2 are not a designed control loop: they control different devices and work against each other.

conflicts.situation: 07:30 on a bright morning: R3 opens the blinds, daylight pushes lux_living above 800, and R1 fires right away.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The blinds open and then close again almost at once. The scheduled morning opening is cancelled and the blinds stay closed for the rest of the day.
conflicts.explanation: R3 sets blinds_living.position to open and R1 sets the same state to closed. Both can fire within moments of each other because opening the blinds is what triggers R1.

conflicts.situation: From 20:00, while the nursery humidifier runs (R1) and nursery humidity rises above 55 %
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The dehumidifier switches on and runs against the humidifier. The two devices fight each other, which wastes energy, keeps humidity swinging and makes noise in the nursery.
conflicts.explanation: R1's humidifier raises humidity_nursery, which makes R2 fire. R2's dehumidifier then cancels out what R1 is trying to do.

conflicts.situation: At or after 20:00, when nursery humidity is above 55 % (for example because the humidifier from R1 is running)
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R5 turns the dehumidifier off for quiet sleep, but R2 turns it back on as soon as humidity goes above 55 %. The loud dehumidifier runs during the baby's sleep, or the device flips between on and off.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules set dehumidifier_nursery.power to opposite values (off vs. on), and their conditions can be true at the same time in the evening.

conflicts.situation: Night mode turns on and R1 switches off the bedroom wall switch. Nothing turns it back on, so it is still off when the wake-up alarm rings the next morning and R2 fires.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The bedroom bulb has no power because it is wired behind the switch. It stays dark, so the wake-up light and the 60 % brightness setting are never applied.
conflicts.explanation: R1 turns off the bedroom wall switch relay, which physically cuts power to the bedroom bulb. R2 depends on that bulb, but neither rule turns the switch back on.

conflicts.situation: Someone arrives home between 17:00 and 19:00, around the 18:00 trigger of R1
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Thermostat is set to both heat/23 C and eco/19 C. Whichever rule fires last wins, so either the evening heating is cancelled or the eco setting is overridden.
conflicts.explanation: R1 and R2 set thermostat.mode and setpoint to incompatible values, and their time windows overlap at 18:00.

conflicts.situation: Living room drops below 20 C, R4 sets heating, and the temperature later rises above 24 C
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Radiator heating and the air conditioner's cooling run at the same time, wasting energy, and the room can swing back and forth between the two.
conflicts.explanation: R4's heating raises temp_living past 24 C, which fires R3's cooling. Neither rule turns the other device off, so they work against each other, and cooling below 20 C fires R4 again.

conflicts.situation: Cold morning with the living room below 20 C around 08:00
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R5 switches the thermostat to eco right after or instead of R4's heat, so the room stays cold. R4 does not fire again because the temperature is already below 20 C.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules set thermostat.mode (heat vs eco) and can both fire on a cold morning.

conflicts.situation: Arrival between 17:00 and 19:00 sets eco at 19 C and the room cools below 20 C
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R4 switches the thermostat back to heat, undoing the eco setting the arrival rule asked for.
conflicts.explanation: R2's eco setpoint of 19 C lets temp_living fall below 20 C, which triggers R4 to set the opposite thermostat mode.

conflicts.situation: Home is in away mode (garage breaker off via R1) and carbon monoxide is detected in the garage (co_garage == true).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 commands the exhaust fan on, but the fan is unpowered because the garage breaker is off, so CO is not ventilated.
conflicts.explanation: The exhaust fan is on the garage circuit; R1 switching the breaker off forces fan_garage.power off, defeating R2's safety action.

conflicts.situation: Home switches to away mode while CO is present in the garage, or CO is detected around the time away mode is set.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Garage door is commanded both open (R2) and closed (R3); if it ends up closed, CO is trapped in the garage.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules target garage_door.position with incompatible values and can fire in overlapping situations.

conflicts.situation: Car is parked in the garage and charging (R4) when the home switches to away mode.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: EV charging is interrupted because the garage breaker is cut, leaving the car uncharged.
conflicts.explanation: The EV charger is on the garage circuit; R1 switching the breaker off forces ev_charger.charging off, undoing R4.

conflicts.situation: At 12:00 while home_mode == away: R1 dispenses cat food, the cat runs to the feeder and trips the kitchen motion sensor (motion_kitchen = true).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 treats the cat's movement as an intruder and sounds the siren. This false alarm happens every day at noon while nobody is home.
conflicts.explanation: The feeder's action sets motion_kitchen to true through the cat (an AFFECTS edge), and that is exactly what triggers R2. R2 cannot tell the cat apart from an intruder.

conflicts.situation: Kitchen motion is detected while home_mode == home (this includes the cat triggering it after R1 dispenses food at noon).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R3 sets camera_kitchen.recording to on and R6 sets it to off at the same moment, so the camera's final state depends on which rule runs last. It may record the occupants even though the privacy rule should stop it.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules fire on the same trigger. R3 has no mode condition, so in home mode it gives camera_kitchen.recording the opposite command to R6.

conflicts.situation: At 23:30, after the home has switched to night mode and R2 has turned the CPAP on (or night mode starts before 23:30)
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Turning off the bedside plug cuts power to the CPAP, so the breathing machine shuts off while the user is asleep. This is a serious health risk.
conflicts.explanation: The CPAP is plugged into the bedside smart plug. R1 turns that plug off to save energy, which also turns off the CPAP that R2 is meant to keep on, and R2 does not fire again until the next switch to night mode.

conflicts.situation: A fall is detected in the bathroom around the time the home switches to night mode (or the mode changes after R3 has already unlocked the door)
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The entrance door ends up locked while an injured person is waiting for help, so paramedics can't get in.
conflicts.explanation: R3 unlocks lock_entrance and R4 locks it. Both can fire close together, and R4 can undo the emergency unlock.

conflicts.situation: At 14:00 the sprinkler starts watering the lawn next to the terrace where the rain sensor is mounted.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The rain sensor reports rain falsely, so the bedroom skylight closes even though it is not raining.
conflicts.explanation: The sprinkler spray wets the terrace rain sensor (rain_sensor set true), which triggers R4's rain response.

conflicts.situation: At 10:00 on a hot day, R2 opens the living room window and outdoor heat raises temp_living above 27 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The AC is switched on to cool a room whose window is open, wasting energy and fighting the incoming hot air.
conflicts.explanation: Opening the window increases temp_living, which crosses R1's trigger threshold and starts AC cooling.

conflicts.situation: Around 10:00 the AC starts cooling (e.g. because the window opened by R2 warmed the room) while R2 wants the window open.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: window_living receives contradictory open/closed commands; the scheduled fresh-air airing is undone or the window oscillates.
conflicts.explanation: R2 sets window_living to open and R6 sets it to closed when the AC cools; both can fire in the same period, especially via the R2->temp rise->R1 chain.

conflicts.situation: Home switches to night mode in the evening (before 01:00); at 01:00 R1 tries to start the NAS backup.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The NAS is unpowered because the closet strip is off, so the nightly backup silently fails or never runs.
conflicts.explanation: R2 turns off the closet power strip, which physically cuts power to the NAS plugged into it. R1's backup command then targets a device that is powered off.

conflicts.situation: Night mode is active (strip off) and the closet temperature rises above 35 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R3's command to turn on the cooling fan has no effect because the fan has no power, so the closet can overheat.
conflicts.explanation: The cooling fan is plugged into the closet strip that R2 switches off, so R3 cannot actually run the fan while the strip is off.

conflicts.situation: The teenager's phone arrives home between 23:00 and 06:00, e.g. coming back late at night.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 unlocks the front door and R2 locks it again straight away. The teenager may be locked out, or the lock may keep switching between unlocked and locked.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules act on lock_front.lock with opposite values. R1's unlock is exactly the event that triggers R2, so during the night window the two rules directly undo each other.

conflicts.situation: Every day at 09:00, both rules trigger simultaneously.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Office shades receive contradictory close and open commands; final position is nondeterministic and the shades may oscillate.
conflicts.explanation: R1 and R6 share the same time trigger and set shades_office.position to opposite values (closed vs. open) with no distinguishing conditions.

conflicts.situation: Winter morning at 09:00 when R1 closes the exterior shades and the office temperature is near 20 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Blocking solar gains cools the office below 20 C, causing R2 to turn on the radiator, so energy is wasted to replace free solar heat.
conflicts.explanation: Closed shades decrease temp_office (blocking winter solar gains), which is the trigger variable of R2 (temp_office < 20), so R1's action indirectly activates heating.

conflicts.situation: From 19:30, when the white-noise speaker starts in the nursery and the baby monitor microphone picks it up, so noise_nursery can go above 60 dB without the baby crying.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The nursery lamp turns on even though the baby is not crying. This can wake the baby or keep it awake.
conflicts.explanation: R2 turns on the white noise, which raises the noise level the monitor measures. R1 reads that level as crying and turns on the lamp.

conflicts.situation: After 20:00, when the TV is turned on and R3 turns on the soundbar. Sound from the soundbar passes through the thin shared wall and pushes noise_nursery above 60 dB.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The nursery lamp turns on during the baby's sleep time because of TV audio, not crying.
conflicts.explanation: The soundbar raises the nursery noise level through the shared wall. R1 then fires on a false crying signal.

conflicts.situation: A frost warning is active in the evening. R1 has turned the greenhouse heater on, and then R6 fires at 22:00. A warning issued after 22:00 also makes the two rules fight over the heater's state.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R6 turns the heater off at 22:00 while the frost warning is still active, so the greenhouse goes unheated through the coldest part of the night and the plants can freeze.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets gh_heater.power to on and R6 sets it to off. Both rules can apply on the same frost night, so they leave the heater in opposite states.

conflicts.situation: A frost warning is active and R1 has turned the heater on. At 22:00, R3 switches off the outdoor plug.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The heater loses power even though R1 still expects it to run, so the greenhouse is left unheated during frost.
conflicts.explanation: The greenhouse heater is plugged into plug_outdoor. When R3 cuts power to that plug, the heater shuts off. This dependency is not stated in either rule.

conflicts.situation: During a frost warning, R1 runs the heater and the greenhouse air warms past 18 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 opens the roof vent while the heater is still running during frost. Warm air escapes into the freezing air outside, which wastes energy, and the temperature swings as the heater keeps running.
conflicts.explanation: The heater raises temp_gh and sets off R2's open-vent action. The open vent then works against the heating that R1 started for frost protection.

conflicts.situation: Night mode is active (or gets switched on) between 22:00 and 06:00, and someone moves in the hallway, e.g. a resident walking to the bathroom or the kitchen.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R3 locks the front door when night mode starts, but R4 unlocks it as soon as there is hallway motion. The door ends up unlocked overnight and the home is not secure.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules set lock_front.lock: R3 sets it to locked and R4 sets it to unlocked. Their trigger windows overlap, because night mode is usually on during R4's 22:00–06:00 window, so either rule can undo the other.

conflicts.situation: At 18:00 while home_mode == away; both rules fire on the same time trigger.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The living room heater gets contradictory on/off commands. Depending on execution order, it may stay on and heat an empty house.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets heater_living.power to on and R5 sets it to off at the same moment. R1 has no condition that excludes away mode, so both rules fire together.

conflicts.situation: After 18:00 the living room heater runs with no rule to turn it off, and temp_living climbs above 26 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The window opens and the ventilation fan runs while the heater is still on, wasting energy as heating and cooling work against each other. The window may also open unexpectedly in the evening.
conflicts.explanation: R1's heater raises the living room temperature until it triggers R2. Nothing turns the heater off, so heating and ventilation run at the same time.

conflicts.situation: Weekdays at 10:00 the robot vacuum starts cleaning and moves through the living room, tripping the living-room PIR sensor (motion_living = true), typically while nobody is home.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The entrance door is unlocked although nobody is home, leaving the house unsecured.
conflicts.explanation: R1's vacuum movement creates false motion in the living room; R2 interprets this as an occupant being home and unlocks the entrance door.

conflicts.situation: Weekdays at 10:00 with home_mode = away, the robot vacuum cleans the living room and triggers motion_living = true.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: False intruder alarm: the indoor siren sounds while the house is empty, causing nuisance or an unnecessary emergency response.
conflicts.explanation: The vacuum started by R1 produces motion that R3 treats as an intrusion during away mode, so the siren is activated.

conflicts.situation: Kitchen smoke is detected (R1 unlocks door) while/after the household mode switches to away (R2 locks door), e.g. occupants leaving or an automated away switch during a smoke event.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The apartment door is re-locked during a smoke/fire event, blocking the evacuation path and responder access.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets lock_door.lock to unlocked and R2 sets it to locked; nothing in R2 checks for smoke, so whichever fires last wins and the evacuation unlock can be undone.

conflicts.situation: Smoke is detected in the kitchen and R1 turns off the air handler; the smoke condition persists until 08:00 when R4 fires.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The central air handler is turned back on during a smoke event, circulating smoke throughout the apartment.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets hvac.power off for safety, while R4 unconditionally sets hvac.power on at 08:00 without checking smoke_kitchen, overriding the safety shutdown.

conflicts.situation: Home switches to night mode while the aquarium water is below 24 C, or the water cools below 24 C during night mode.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Aquarium heater gets opposite commands: R5 turns it off for quiet, R2 turns it back on. Either the night-quiet goal fails or the fish are left in water that is too cold.
conflicts.explanation: R5 sets aquarium_heater.power to off on night mode, and R2 sets it to on when water_temp < 24. Switching the heater off makes the water cool, which triggers R2, so the two rules fight over the same device.

conflicts.situation: Home is in away mode (main valve closed by R1) and the clock reaches 06:00, triggering R2.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Irrigation is switched on but receives no water; the garden is not watered during the absence while the controller reports flow/watering as on.
conflicts.explanation: The garden irrigation is supplied through the main water line. Closing valve_main cuts the supply the sprinkler relies on, a dependency not stated in either rule.

conflicts.situation: A leak in the utility room has closed the main valve (R3) and it reaches 06:00 before the valve is reopened.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Scheduled watering silently fails (irrigation 'on' with no water); restoring watering would require reopening the main valve, undermining leak protection.
conflicts.explanation: R2's irrigation physically depends on water from the main supply that R3 shuts off, so the safety shut-off quietly disables the watering schedule.

conflicts.situation: Daytime with strong sunlight: lux_living rises above 800, R1 closes blinds_living, and indoor illuminance then falls below 150 lux.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 switches on the living room ceiling lights in broad daylight, replacing free daylight with electric light and wasting energy; nothing reopens the blinds, so the lights stay on.
conflicts.explanation: R1's action (closing the blinds) lowers lux_living, the environment variable that triggers R2, so the glare-reduction rule indirectly causes the lights to turn on.

conflicts.situation: At 07:30 on a bright morning: R3 opens blinds_living, sunlight pushes lux_living above 800, and R1 closes the blinds.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The blinds open and then close almost immediately, so the scheduled morning opening is cancelled and the user doesn't get the open blinds R3 was meant to give them.
conflicts.explanation: R3 and R1 set opposite values on blinds_living.position, and opening the blinds (R3) raises the illuminance that triggers R1 to close them.

conflicts.situation: From 20:00, when R1 turns on the nursery humidifier and nursery humidity rises above 55 %
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The dehumidifier switches on and runs against the humidifier all night: wasted energy, no stable humidity, and a loud dehumidifier in the nursery during sleep
conflicts.explanation: R1's humidifier raises humidity_nursery, which meets R2's trigger (>55 %). R2 then starts the dehumidifier, which works against R1's goal.

conflicts.situation: At or after 20:00, when nursery humidity is or becomes above 55 % (for example because of the humidifier)
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The dehumidifier is switched off at 20:00 and then back on by R2 (or the order flips), so it runs loudly during the baby's sleep
conflicts.explanation: R5 sets dehumidifier_nursery.power to off and R2 sets it to on. Both can be active in the same evening period, so they give opposite commands to the same device.

conflicts.situation: Night mode turns the bedroom in-wall relay switch off (R1). Later the wake-up alarm rings (R2) and nothing has turned the switch back on.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The bedroom smart bulb has no mains power, so it cannot turn on or fade to 60 %. The wake-up light does not come on.
conflicts.explanation: The bedroom in-wall smart relay switch most likely supplies power to the bedroom smart bulb. When R1 cuts that relay, the bulb goes offline and R2's on and brightness commands fail. Neither rule mentions this link.

conflicts.situation: Someone arrives home between 17:00 and 19:00 (before or after 18:00), so both R1 (18:00) and R2 fire within the same window.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Thermostat flips between heat/23 C and eco/19 C; the final state depends on which rule fired last, so either comfort or energy saving is lost.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets thermostat to heat 23 C at 18:00 while R2 sets it to eco 19 C on arrival during 17:00-19:00; both target the same thermostat mode/setpoint with incompatible values.

conflicts.situation: After an arrival between 17:00 and 19:00, R2 sets eco at 19 C and the living room temperature drifts below 20 C (or is already below 20 C).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R4 switches the thermostat back to heat, overriding the intended eco setting; the thermostat oscillates between eco and heat.
conflicts.explanation: R2's eco setpoint of 19 C lets temp_living fall below 20 C, which triggers R4 to set heat mode, defeating R2's eco intent.

conflicts.situation: At 08:00 R5 sets eco mode while the living room is cold or later cools below 20 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Thermostat toggles between eco and heat in the morning; the eco schedule is defeated or R4's heating request is overridden at 08:00.
conflicts.explanation: R5 lowers heating to eco, which lets temp_living fall below 20 C and triggers R4 to set heat; if it is already cold, R5 directly overrides R4's heat mode.

conflicts.situation: Carbon monoxide is detected in the garage (co_garage == true) around the time the home switches to away mode.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The garage door gets contradictory commands (open vs. closed). If R3 wins, the door closes and CO builds up in a sealed garage.
conflicts.explanation: R2 opens garage_door to vent CO and R3 closes the same door when the home switches to away mode. Both can fire together and send opposite commands to garage_door.position.

conflicts.situation: The home is in away mode, so the garage breaker is off, and CO is then detected in the garage.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The exhaust fan and the garage door opener have no power, so CO can't be vented and stays trapped in the garage.
conflicts.explanation: R1 turns off breaker_garage, which most likely powers the garage circuit with fan_garage and the garage door opener. R2's safety actions then silently fail.

conflicts.situation: Both rules fire at the same moment when home_mode changes to away; the breaker may go off before the door finishes closing.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The garage door motor loses power and the door is left open or half-open while the home is empty, which is a security risk.
conflicts.explanation: The garage door opener most likely runs on the garage circuit that R1 cuts. A race between R1 and R3 can stop the door from closing.

conflicts.situation: The car is parked in the garage while the home is in away mode, for example if the residents left another way or the car arrives before away mode ends.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: EV charging stops or never starts, so the car is not charged when needed.
conflicts.explanation: The wall-box EV charger most likely runs on the garage circuit, which R1 switches off. R4's charging command then has no effect.

conflicts.situation: Kitchen motion detected (motion_kitchen == true) while home_mode == home
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R3 turns kitchen camera recording on while R6 turns it off at the same moment; final state is nondeterministic, either violating privacy or flickering
conflicts.explanation: Both rules share the same trigger and R3 has no mode condition, so in home mode both fire and issue opposite commands to camera_kitchen.recording.

conflicts.situation: A fall is detected in the bathroom (fall_detected == true) and R3 unlocks the entrance door; the home then switches to night mode (home_mode == night), or both events happen close together in the evening.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R4 re-locks the entrance door during a medical emergency, so paramedics cannot get in to reach the person who fell.
conflicts.explanation: R3 sets lock_entrance to unlocked for emergency access, while R4 sets the same lock to locked on night mode without checking for an active fall. The two rules give opposite commands to the same device, and whichever fires last wins.

conflicts.situation: At 10:00 on a warm day while the living room AC is (or starts) cooling because temp_living > 27 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: window_living is commanded open by R2 and closed by R6. If the AC was already cooling, R6 does not fire again, so the window stays open while the AC runs and energy is wasted. Otherwise the scheduled fresh-air opening is undone right away.
conflicts.explanation: R2 opens the living room window at a fixed time, ignoring the AC state. R6 closes the same window whenever the AC starts cooling, so the two rules give opposite commands to one actuator when both apply.

conflicts.situation: At 14:00 on a dry day, when the sprinkler next to the terrace waters the lawn and its spray reaches the rain sensor mounted on the terrace.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The rain sensor falsely reports rain and R4 closes the bedroom skylight unexpectedly every watering day, cutting off ventilation.
conflicts.explanation: The sprinkler's water changes the rain sensor reading, which falsely triggers R4's rain-closing rule.

conflicts.situation: Home is in night mode (strip_closet turned off) when R1 starts the NAS backup at 01:00.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The NAS has no power because it runs off the closet strip, so the nightly backup never starts or stops partway.
conflicts.explanation: R2 turns off the closet power strip, which likely powers the NAS in the same closet. R1 depends on the NAS being powered, a dependency the rules don't state.

conflicts.situation: Night mode has turned off the closet strip, and the closet temperature rises above 35 C (for example while the NAS is running).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R3 sends the fan its 'on' command, but the fan has no power, so the closet overheats and equipment may be damaged.
conflicts.explanation: The closet cooling fan is likely plugged into the closet power strip. Turning off the strip in night mode silently stops R3's cooling from working.

conflicts.situation: The teenager's phone arrives home between 23:00 and 06:00.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 unlocks the front door, then R2 sees it unlocked and locks it again right away. The door flips between unlocked and locked, and the teenager may be locked out or find the door locked again while opening it.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules act on lock_front.lock with opposite values. R1's action is exactly what triggers R2 during the night window, so the door can't stay unlocked for the teenager arriving late.

conflicts.situation: Every day at 09:00, when both time triggers fire at once.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The office shades get opposite commands (closed and open). They end up in whichever position was set last, so they may fail to block glare for screen work or fail to let in daylight.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules have the same trigger (time == 09:00) and no conditions, but they set shades_office.position to opposite values (closed vs. open).

conflicts.situation: From 19:30 onward, after R2 starts the white-noise speaker in the nursery and its output pushes the baby monitor's measured noise_nursery above 60 dB.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 interprets the white noise as the baby crying and turns on the nursery lamp. This can repeat all evening and may wake the sleeping baby, so the false trigger defeats both the white noise and the crying alert.
conflicts.explanation: The white-noise speaker is in the nursery and raises the sound level the baby monitor measures. R1 cannot tell crying from white noise, so R2's action triggers R1 unexpectedly.

conflicts.situation: A frost warning is active at or before 22:00; R1 has switched the greenhouse heater on, then R6 fires at 22:00.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The heater is switched off during a frost night, leaving the plants exposed to frost damage.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets gh_heater.power to on and R6 sets it to off. Both can apply on the same frost evening, and R1 does not re-fire while the warning stays active.

conflicts.situation: During a frost warning the heater runs (R1) with no off rule until 22:00, and the greenhouse temperature rises above 18 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 opens the roof vent and lets freezing outside air in while the heater keeps running. This wastes energy and undermines the frost protection.
conflicts.explanation: The heater's warming changes temp_gh, which triggers R2's vent opening. The vent opening then works against the heater's goal of protecting the greenhouse from frost.

conflicts.situation: At night (22:00–06:00) the home is in night mode, so R3 has locked the front door, and then the hallway sensor detects motion (for example a resident walking past or someone near the door).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R4 unlocks the front door that R3 just locked. The door stays unlocked overnight, and the order in which the rules fire decides whether it ends up locked or unlocked.
conflicts.explanation: R3 sets lock_front to locked when night mode starts, and R4 sets the same lock to unlocked on any hallway motion during the same night window. Both rules can fire in the same situation and give opposite commands to one device.

conflicts.situation: At 18:00 while home_mode == away
conflicts.undesired_outcome: heater_living receives both 'on' and 'off' at the same moment; final state is nondeterministic and the heater may run in an empty house
conflicts.explanation: Both rules trigger at 18:00 on the same device with opposite actions; R1 has no away-mode exclusion, so both fire when the home is away.

conflicts.situation: Evening after 18:00 when R1's heater raises temp_living above 26 C
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Window opens and fan runs while the heater keeps heating, wasting energy and causing the rules to work against each other
conflicts.explanation: R1's heating raises temp_living, which triggers R2 to open the window and ventilate, but nothing turns the heater off, so heating and cooling run at the same time.

conflicts.situation: temp_living < 19 C turns heater on, it heats past 26 C (R2 opens window), then the open window cools the room below 19 C again
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Heater runs with the window open, and the room may swing back and forth between heating and venting, wasting energy
conflicts.explanation: R4 starts the heater with no stop rule, so heating triggers R2. R2's open window then lowers the temperature and can re-trigger R4, so the two rules keep working against each other.

conflicts.situation: Home in away mode; after R5 turns the heater off at 18:00, temp_living falls below 19 C
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Heater is switched back on in away mode, undoing R5's away shutoff and heating an empty house
