conflicts.explanation: R4 has no away-mode condition, so it sets heater_living to on and overrides R5's away-mode off command on the same device.

conflicts.situation: Weekdays at 10:00, when the robot vacuum starts cleaning in the living room, often while nobody is home.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The living-room motion sensor picks up the moving vacuum and the entrance door unlocks, leaving the house open while it is empty.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sends the vacuum through the living room, which sets motion_living to true. R2 takes that motion to mean someone is home and unlocks the entrance door.

conflicts.situation: Weekdays at 10:00 while the home is in away mode and the vacuum starts cleaning the living room.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: False intruder alarm: the indoor siren sounds because of the vacuum, not a person.
conflicts.explanation: The vacuum's movement sets off the living-room motion sensor. With home_mode set to away, R3 reads this as an intrusion and turns on the siren.

conflicts.situation: Kitchen smoke is detected and R1 has turned the air handler off; smoke is still present, or still being handled, when 08:00 arrives.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R4 turns the air handler back on, undoing the safety shutdown and possibly spreading smoke through the apartment.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets hvac.power to off and R4 sets hvac.power to on. R4 has no smoke condition, so both can apply at the same time.

conflicts.situation: Kitchen smoke is detected while the home is in away mode, or the home switches to away mode while smoke is still present.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The door either ends up unlocked while nobody is home, or ends up locked during a smoke or fire emergency, which may block the exit or keep firefighters out.
conflicts.explanation: R1 unlocks lock_door and R2 locks it. Neither rule checks the other's condition, so whichever fires last decides the lock state.

conflicts.situation: Home is in night mode and the aquarium water temperature is below 24 C (or drops below it while the heater is off overnight).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The aquarium heater is commanded both off (R5) and on (R2): either the quiet-night goal is defeated, or the heater stays off and the fish are exposed to too-cold water.
conflicts.explanation: R5 switches the heater off at night; with the heater off the water cools below 24 C, which makes R2 switch the same heater back on, giving contradictory on/off commands on aquarium_heater.power.

conflicts.situation: Home is in away mode, so R1 has closed the main water valve; at 06:00 R2 turns irrigation flow and watering on.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The irrigation runs without water: the garden isn't watered while the occupants are away, and the controller or pump may run dry.
conflicts.explanation: The garden irrigation is supplied through the main shut-off valve. R2 turns the irrigation on without checking that valve, so closing it (R1) silently defeats R2.

conflicts.situation: A leak in the utility room has triggered R3 and closed the main valve; at 06:00 R2 starts watering.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Irrigation is commanded on with no water supply. Watering fails, the controller may run dry, and reopening the valve to let watering run would undo the leak protection.
conflicts.explanation: R2's action depends on the main valve being open, but R3 shuts that valve as a safety measure. Nothing in R2 accounts for this.

conflicts.situation: Sunny daytime when lux_living exceeds 800 and R1 closes the blinds
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Closing the blinds makes lux_living fall below 150, so R2 turns on the ceiling lights during bright daylight, which wastes energy
conflicts.explanation: R1's action (closing the blinds) changes the living-room light level, which triggers R2. Glare control ends up replacing daylight with electric light.

conflicts.situation: 07:30 on a bright morning: R3 opens the blinds and lux_living rises above 800
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 closes the blinds right after R3 opens them, so the scheduled morning opening is undone and the blinds may move back and forth
conflicts.explanation: Both rules set blinds_living.position to opposite values (open vs. closed) in the same situation, and R3's opening is what causes R1 to fire.

conflicts.situation: At 20:00 R1 turns on the nursery humidifier; nursery humidity then rises above 55 %.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 turns on the dehumidifier, so the humidifier and dehumidifier run against each other all night. This wastes energy, adds noise in the nursery and makes humidity swing.
conflicts.explanation: The humidifier started by R1 raises nursery humidity past R2's threshold, so R2 starts a device that undoes R1's goal.

conflicts.situation: After 20:00, R5 has switched the nursery dehumidifier off, and then nursery humidity goes above 55 % (for example because of R1's humidifier).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 switches the loud dehumidifier back on during the baby's sleep, defeating R5.
conflicts.explanation: R2 and R5 set dehumidifier_nursery.power to opposite values, and their conditions can both be true at night, so whichever fires last controls the device.

conflicts.situation: Home is in night mode (bedroom wall switch turned off by R1) when the wake-up alarm rings in the morning.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 tries to fade in the bedroom bulb to 60%, but the bulb has no power because the in-wall relay is off, so the wake-up light does not come on.
conflicts.explanation: The bedroom in-wall relay switch likely supplies power to the bedroom smart bulb. R1 cuts that power, so R2's command to the bulb cannot take effect.

conflicts.situation: Around 18:00 when someone arrives home within the 17:00-19:00 window (e.g. arrival at 18:05 or just before 18:00).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Thermostat is set to both heat/23 C and eco/19 C; the last rule wins, so the scheduled warm evening is cancelled or the eco setting is immediately overridden.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets thermostat.mode=heat, setpoint=23 at 18:00, while R2 sets mode=eco, setpoint=19 on arrival in a window containing 18:00. Both write incompatible values to the same thermostat states.

conflicts.situation: Someone arrives between 17:00 and 19:00 while the living room is below 20 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Thermostat toggles between eco (19 C) and heat; the room may stay cold or the thermostat oscillates.
conflicts.explanation: R4 demands heat mode when temp_living < 20 while R2 sets eco mode with a 19 C setpoint on arrival; the eco setpoint lets temperature stay/fall below 20, re-triggering R4.

conflicts.situation: Cold morning: living room below 20 C around 08:00.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R5 switches the thermostat to eco at 08:00, overriding the heat mode R4 requested, leaving the room cold.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules write thermostat.mode with incompatible values (heat vs. eco) and R5 has no temperature condition, so both can be active at the same time.

conflicts.situation: CO is detected in the garage while the home is in (or switches to) away mode
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The garage door gets both open and close commands. It may end up closed so CO isn't vented, or open so the home isn't secure.
conflicts.explanation: R2 sets garage_door to open and R3 sets it to closed. Both can fire at the same time.

conflicts.situation: The home is in away mode (garage breaker off) and CO is detected in the garage
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The exhaust fan and door opener have no power, so the CO emergency response fails.
conflicts.explanation: R1 cuts the garage circuit. The fan and door opener presumably run on that circuit, so R2's actions have no effect.

conflicts.situation: The home switches to away mode and both rules fire. The breaker cuts power before the door finishes closing.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The garage door stays open while the household is away.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules start on the same event in no fixed order. Cutting the garage breaker can take power away from the door opener that R3 needs.

conflicts.situation: The car is parked in the garage while the home is in away mode
conflicts.undesired_outcome: EV charging is started but gets no power, so the car isn't charged.
conflicts.explanation: The breaker that R1 turns off feeds the wall-box charger that R4 tries to start.

conflicts.situation: Kitchen motion is detected while home_mode == home
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Kitchen camera recording is turned on and off at the same time; it may end up recording the household against the privacy rule, or flip between on and off
conflicts.explanation: R3 has no mode condition and sets camera_kitchen.recording to on for any kitchen motion. R6 sets it to off on the same trigger in home mode, so both fire together with opposite commands.

conflicts.situation: A fall is detected (fall_detected == true) and the entrance door is unlocked for paramedics; then, before help arrives, home_mode switches to night (e.g., scheduled or routine-driven).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The entrance door is re-locked while the fallen occupant awaits paramedics, blocking emergency access.
conflicts.explanation: R3 sets lock_entrance to unlocked on fall detection and R4 sets it to locked on night mode. Neither rule checks the other's context, so whichever fires last wins, and the safety-critical unlock can be overridden.

conflicts.situation: At 10:00 while the living room AC is already in cool mode (temp_living > 27 C since earlier).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The living room window is opened while the AC is cooling and stays open, wasting energy and undermining cooling.
conflicts.explanation: R6 closes window_living only at the moment the AC switches to cool; R2 later opens the same window at 10:00 and R6 does not re-fire, so open and closed commands clash on the same device.

conflicts.situation: At 14:00 when the lawn sprinkler, located next to the terrace, starts watering.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The bedroom skylight closes even though it is not raining.
conflicts.explanation: The sprinkler's spray can wet the rain sensor mounted on the terrace, making rain_sensor true and triggering R4 to close the skylight.

conflicts.situation: Home is in night mode (strip_closet turned off by R2) and at 01:00 R1 starts the nightly NAS backup.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The NAS, located in the closet and powered via the closet power strip, has no power, so the backup fails, or a running backup is cut off abruptly, risking data corruption.
conflicts.explanation: R2 cuts power to the closet power strip, which the closet NAS depends on. R1 needs the NAS powered to run the backup, but this dependency isn't stated in either rule.

conflicts.situation: Night mode is active (strip_closet off) and the closet temperature rises above 35 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R3 turns on the closet cooling fan, but it is unpowered, so the closet keeps overheating and the equipment there may be damaged.
conflicts.explanation: The closet fan is likely supplied by the closet power strip. Once R2 switches the strip off, R3's fan-on command has no effect.

conflicts.situation: The teenager's phone arrives home between 23:00 and 06:00 (for example, coming home late at night).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 unlocks the front door, and R2 locks it again right away. The door keeps switching between locked and unlocked, and the teenager may be locked out, or the door may end up in a state nobody intended.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules set lock_front.lock on the same device to opposite values. R1's unlock is exactly what triggers R2 during the night window, so the two actions cancel each other out.

conflicts.situation: Every day at 09:00, both time-triggered rules fire simultaneously with no further conditions.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: shades_office receives contradictory commands (closed vs open); final position depends on execution order and may oscillate.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets shades_office.position to closed and R6 sets it to open on the identical trigger time == 09:00, so the actions are directly incompatible.

conflicts.situation: At 19:30 R2 starts the white-noise speaker in the nursery. The baby monitor picks up the white noise, and the nursery sound level (noise_nursery) can go above 60 dB while the baby is calm or asleep.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 reads the white noise as crying and turns on the nursery lamp at bedtime. The light can wake the baby, and the lamp may stay on all night because the white noise keeps the sound level high.
conflicts.explanation: R2's speaker raises the same sound level that R1 uses to detect crying. As a result, R1 fires when the baby isn't crying, and it can no longer tell real crying apart from the white noise.

conflicts.situation: A frost warning is active (frost_warning == true) and R1 has turned the greenhouse heater on. At 22:00, while the warning is still in effect, R6 fires.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The greenhouse heater is switched off on a frost night, in the coldest hours, so the plants can be damaged by frost.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets gh_heater.power to on and R6 sets it to off. Both can be in effect at the same time because nothing in R6 checks the frost warning, so the 22:00 schedule overrides the frost protection.

conflicts.situation: During a frost warning, R1 turns the heater on and the greenhouse air warms above 18 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The roof vent opens to freezing outside air during the frost. The heat that was built up escapes, energy is wasted and frost protection is weaker. The heater and vent may also keep cycling against each other.
conflicts.explanation: The heater turned on by R1 raises temp_gh, which triggers R2 to open the vent. R2 does not check whether a frost warning is active, so the heating action leads to a venting action that works against it.

conflicts.situation: At night (22:00–06:00) the home is in night mode and R3 has locked the front door. Then someone moves in the hallway, for example a resident going to the bathroom or the person who just set night mode.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R4 unlocks the front door that R3 just locked, so the apartment stays unlocked overnight even though it is in night mode.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules set lock_front.lock to opposite values (locked vs. unlocked), and their triggers overlap at night. Hallway motion is very likely while night mode is on, so R4 undoes R3's security action.

conflicts.situation: At 18:00 while home_mode == away
conflicts.undesired_outcome: heater_living is commanded both on and off at the same moment; the result depends on execution order and the heater may run in an empty house
conflicts.explanation: Both rules fire on the same trigger. R5's away-mode condition doesn't stop R1 from firing, so the two actions on heater_living.power contradict each other.

conflicts.situation: After 18:00 the living room heater stays on (no rule turns it off) until temp_living rises above 26 C
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The window opens and the fan starts while the heater keeps running, wasting energy as heat is vented outside
conflicts.explanation: R1's heating pushes the temperature past R2's threshold. R2 opens the window and starts the fan but doesn't turn the heater off, so heating and venting run at the same time.

conflicts.situation: After R2 opens the living room window (temp > 26 C), outside air cools the room below 19 C
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R4 turns the heater on while the window is still open and the fan is running, so the house heats and vents at once
conflicts.explanation: R2's open window lowers temp_living, which triggers R4. No rule closes the window or turns off the heater, so the two rules keep working against each other.

conflicts.situation: Weekdays at 10:00, when the robot vacuum starts cleaning and moves through the living room, usually while the household is out.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The entrance door unlocks while nobody is home, so the house is left open.
conflicts.explanation: The moving vacuum trips the living-room PIR sensor (motion_living = true). R2 reads that as a person being home and unlocks the entrance door.

conflicts.situation: Weekdays at 10:00 with home_mode = away, while the vacuum is cleaning the living room.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: A false intrusion alarm: the indoor siren sounds with no intruder present.
conflicts.explanation: The vacuum's movement sets motion_living = true. Because the home is in away mode, R3 treats this as an intruder and turns the siren on.

conflicts.situation: Smoke is detected in the kitchen (smoke_kitchen == true) and R1 unlocks the door for evacuation. During the smoke event, home_mode changes to away, for example from a geofence update or a scheduled mode change.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 locks the apartment door while there is still smoke, which undoes the evacuation unlock. People inside or firefighters may be blocked.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules set lock_door.lock to opposite values (unlocked vs locked). Neither rule has a condition that rules out the other, so the one that fires last decides the lock state.

conflicts.situation: Smoke is detected in the kitchen and R1 turns off the air handler. At 08:00, while smoke is still present, R4 fires.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R4 turns the central air handler back on during a smoke or fire event. This can spread smoke through the apartment and feed the fire.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets hvac.power to off and R4 sets it to on. R4 is time-based and does not check smoke_kitchen, so it can override the safety shutdown.

conflicts.situation: In night mode, while the aquarium water temperature is below 24 C or falls below 24 C during the night (more likely because R5 has turned the heater off).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R5 turns the aquarium heater off for quiet. R2 then turns it back on, so the heater keeps switching between off and on. Either the quiet-night goal fails, or the fish get water that is too cold if R5 wins.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules set aquarium_heater.power to opposite values, and they can both apply at the same time. R5 also causes the temperature drop that sets off R2.

conflicts.situation: Home is in away mode (R1 has closed the main water valve) and the clock reaches 06:00, so R2 starts irrigation.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The sprinkler is switched on but gets no water because the main valve is shut. The garden goes unwatered while the occupants are away, and the controller wrongly reports that it is watering.
conflicts.explanation: Irrigation draws water downstream of the motorised main shut-off valve, a dependency not stated in R2. R1 cuts that supply, so R2's action can't take effect.

conflicts.situation: The utility-room leak sensor has triggered R3, closing the main valve. At 06:00 R2 starts the garden irrigation.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Irrigation runs dry: the controller says it is watering but there is no flow, so the garden misses its scheduled watering until someone reopens the main valve.
conflicts.explanation: The sprinkler depends on water passing through the main valve. R3's leak shut-off silently stops the supply that R2 relies on.

conflicts.situation: At 07:30 on a sunny morning, when opening the blinds lets in enough daylight to push lux_living above 800.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The blinds R3 just opened are closed again by R1, so the scheduled morning opening is cancelled and the blinds move back and forth.
conflicts.explanation: R3 opens the blinds, which raises the living-room light level. Above 800 lux this triggers R1, which closes the blinds, the opposite of R3's action.

conflicts.situation: Daytime with strong sunlight: lux_living goes above 800 and R1 closes the blinds, which can drop the room below 150 lux.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The ceiling lights turn on during the day while it's bright outside, wasting energy and working against the reason the blinds were closed.
conflicts.explanation: R1's blind closing reduces living-room light. When it falls below 150 lux, R2 fires and turns on the artificial lights.

conflicts.situation: At 20:00 R1 turns on the nursery humidifier; nursery humidity rises above 55 %.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 turns on the dehumidifier, so the humidifier and dehumidifier run against each other all night. This wastes energy, makes humidity swing up and down, and puts a loud compressor in the nursery while the baby sleeps.
conflicts.explanation: The humidifier R1 starts raises nursery humidity, which is exactly what triggers R2 to start the dehumidifier. The two devices end up undoing each other's work.

conflicts.situation: After 20:00, when R5 has turned the dehumidifier off for sleep, nursery humidity goes above 55 % (made more likely by R1's humidifier).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 turns the dehumidifier back on during the night, undoing R5's off command, and the noise disturbs the baby's sleep.
conflicts.explanation: R5 sets dehumidifier_nursery.power to off and R2 sets it to on. R2 has no time restriction, so both can fire in the same evening and give opposite commands to the same device.

conflicts.situation: The home switches to night mode in the evening and R1 turns off the bedroom in-wall relay switch. Next morning the wake-up alarm rings while the switch is still off, and R2 tries to fade the bedroom bulb in to 60 %.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The bedroom bulb has no power, so it ignores R2's on/brightness command. The wake-up light does not come on.
conflicts.explanation: The in-wall relay switch in the bedroom most likely powers the bedroom smart bulb. R1 cuts that power and no rule turns it back on, so R2's command reaches a bulb that is switched off at the wall.

conflicts.situation: Someone arrives home between 17:00 and 19:00, around the 18:00 schedule of R1
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Thermostat is set to heat/23 C by R1 and eco/19 C by R2; the last rule wins, either cancelling the evening heat-up or overriding the arrival eco setting
conflicts.explanation: Both rules write incompatible values to thermostat.mode and thermostat.setpoint in an overlapping time window.

conflicts.situation: After an arrival between 17:00 and 19:00, R2 sets eco at 19 C and the living room temperature falls below 20 C (or is already below 20 C)
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R4 switches the thermostat back to heat, undoing the eco setting; the rules override each other
conflicts.explanation: R2's eco setpoint of 19 C lets temp_living drop below 20 C, which triggers R4 to set the thermostat to heat, the opposite of what R2 intended.

conflicts.situation: At 08:00 R5 sets eco mode and the living room then cools below 20 C (or is already below 20 C)
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R4 immediately puts the thermostat back in heat mode, defeating the morning eco setting
conflicts.explanation: Eco mode lowers the living room temperature below 20 C, which triggers R4 to set heat, reversing R5's action.

conflicts.situation: Home is in away mode (the garage breaker is off) and carbon monoxide is detected in the garage.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The exhaust fan and the motorised garage door have no power, so the garage is not ventilated and CO builds up. This is a safety hazard.
conflicts.explanation: R1 cuts power to the whole garage circuit. R2 needs the fan and door opener on that circuit to clear the CO, so its commands fail without anyone noticing.

conflicts.situation: The home switches to away mode, which triggers R1 and R3 at the same time.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: If the breaker turns off before the door finishes closing, the door stays open while nobody is home. This is a security risk.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules have the same trigger. The garage door opener runs on the garage circuit that R1 switches off, so whether R3 succeeds depends on which action runs first.

conflicts.situation: CO is detected in the garage while or just before the home switches to away mode.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 opens the garage door and R3 closes it. Either the door ends up closed and traps the CO, or it ends up open and leaves the house unsecured.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules can fire at the same time and send opposite commands to garage_door.position.

conflicts.situation: The car is parked in the garage while the home is in away mode, for example when residents leave without the car or the car arrives before the mode changes.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: EV charging does not start, or stops, so the car is not charged when it is needed.
conflicts.explanation: R4 starts the wall-box charger, but R1 has cut power to the garage circuit it depends on.

conflicts.situation: The car arrives in the garage while the home is still in away mode and the garage breaker is off.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The garage light does not turn on, so the driver has to park and move around in the dark.
conflicts.explanation: R5 turns on the garage light, but the light has no power because R1 switched off the garage breaker.

conflicts.situation: Kitchen motion is detected (motion_kitchen == true) while home_mode == home.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The kitchen camera gets both recording := on (R3) and recording := off (R6). It either records the occupants and breaks the privacy setting, or recording is cancelled, depending on which rule runs last.
conflicts.explanation: R3 has no mode condition, so it fires on every kitchen motion event, including in home mode. In that mode R6 fires on the same trigger and sets the same camera state to the opposite value.

conflicts.situation: A fall is detected in the bathroom in the evening, and R3 unlocks the entrance door. Before the paramedics arrive, or at about the same moment, the home switches to night mode.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R4 locks the entrance door again after R3 unlocked it. Paramedics can't get in to help the person who fell, which delays emergency care.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules set lock_entrance.lock, one to unlocked and one to locked. They have independent triggers that can happen close together, and neither rule has a condition that rules out the other.

conflicts.situation: On a hot day, the living room is above 27 C, so R1 has set ac_living.mode to cool, and the time reaches 10:00.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The living room window is opened while the AC is cooling. Because R6 only fires when cooling starts, nothing closes the window again, so the AC cools an open room and wastes energy. If R2 runs first instead, R6 closes the window as soon as cooling starts and the fresh air is lost.
conflicts.explanation: R2 sets window_living to open at 10:00 and R6 sets it to closed whenever the AC is cooling. Both can apply in the same period, so the window gets contradictory commands.

conflicts.situation: At 14:00 the sprinkler next to the terrace starts watering in dry weather while the bedroom skylight is open.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The rain sensor reports rain that isn't happening, and the bedroom skylight closes without a reason. Any ventilation it was giving is lost.
conflicts.explanation: Spray from the sprinkler (R3) wets the rain sensor on the terrace and sets rain_sensor to true. That falsely triggers R4, which closes the skylight.

conflicts.situation: Home is in night mode (closet power strip turned off by R2) when the clock reaches 01:00 and R1 starts the NAS backup.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The NAS, which is likely powered from the closet power strip, has no power. The nightly backup fails or is cut off midway, which could corrupt the backup or the disks.
conflicts.explanation: R2 turns off the closet power strip, which likely feeds the NAS in the same closet. R1 depends on the NAS being powered, but this dependency isn't stated in either rule.

conflicts.situation: Night mode is active (strip off) and the closet temperature rises above 35 °C, for example during the 01:00 backup.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The closet cooling fan, likely plugged into the closet power strip, can't run. The closet overheats and the equipment is put at risk.
conflicts.explanation: R3 turns on the fan, but the fan probably gets its power from the strip that R2 switched off, so the cooling action has no effect.

conflicts.situation: The teenager's phone arrives home between 23:00 and 06:00, e.g. coming back late at night.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 unlocks the front door and R2 locks it again straight away. The teenager may be locked out, or the lock may keep switching between unlocked and locked.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules act on lock_front.lock with opposite values. R1's unlock is exactly the event that triggers R2, so during the night window the two rules directly undo each other.

conflicts.situation: Every day at 09:00, both rules trigger simultaneously on the office shades.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Shades receive both 'closed' and 'open' commands; final position is nondeterministic and may oscillate, defeating either screen-glare protection or daylight use.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets shades_office.position to closed and R6 sets it to open on the identical trigger time == 09:00 with no distinguishing conditions.

conflicts.situation: From 19:30 on, when the white-noise speaker in the nursery is playing near the baby monitor and the measured nursery sound level goes above 60 dB.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The nursery lamp turns on even though the baby isn't crying. This lights up the room while the baby is trying to sleep and may wake them.
conflicts.explanation: R2's white-noise speaker adds sound to the nursery, which raises noise_nursery, the value R1 uses to detect crying. White noise loud enough to pass 60 dB looks like crying to R1, so the lamp turns on by mistake.

conflicts.situation: A frost warning is issued before 22:00 and is still active at 22:00.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R6 turns the greenhouse heater off during the frost warning, so plants may be damaged by frost overnight.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets gh_heater.power to on when frost is forecast, and R6 sets it to off at 22:00 regardless of conditions. R1 doesn't fire again because the warning hasn't changed, so the heater stays off.

conflicts.situation: A frost warning is active, R1 turns the heater on, and the greenhouse air rises above 18 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The roof vent opens during frost, letting cold air in and wasting heater energy.
conflicts.explanation: R1's heating raises temp_gh past R2's 18 C threshold, which opens the vent while it's freezing outside and works against the frost protection R1 is meant to give.

conflicts.situation: Night mode is on (front door locked by R3) and motion is detected in the hallway between 22:00 and 06:00, e.g. a resident walking through the hallway at night.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The front door is unlocked during the night, which undoes the night-mode lock and leaves the apartment unsecured.
conflicts.explanation: R3 sets lock_front to locked when night mode starts, and R4 sets the same lock to unlocked on any hallway motion during night hours. Both can fire in the same period, so they give the lock opposite commands.

conflicts.situation: The home is in away mode after 23:00 (or switches to away mode then), and the hallway camera is powered through the hallway smart plug.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: At 23:00 the hallway camera loses power and stops recording while nobody is home, so the away-mode surveillance stops working without anyone noticing.
conflicts.explanation: R1 turns off plug_hall to save energy. If the hallway camera gets its power from that plug, this cancels R2's recording, because neither rule mentions that the camera depends on the plug. This assumes the camera is plugged into the hallway plug, which the rules do not state.

conflicts.situation: At 18:00 while home_mode == away
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Living room heater is commanded both on and off at the same moment; final state depends on execution order, possibly leaving the heater running in an empty house.
conflicts.explanation: R1 and R5 share the same trigger (18:00) and R5's condition does not exclude R1, so they issue contradictory power commands to heater_living.

conflicts.situation: Evening after 18:00, heater_living turned on by R1 heats the living room above 26 C
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Window opens and fan runs while the heater keeps heating, wasting energy and fighting each other.
conflicts.explanation: R1's heater raises temp_living, which triggers R2; R2 does not turn the heater off, so heating and venting run simultaneously.

conflicts.situation: Heater turned on by R4 (temp < 19 C) pushes temp above 26 C; R2 opens the window, temperature drops below 19 C again
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Heater runs against an open window and fan; the room oscillates between heating and venting, wasting energy.
conflicts.explanation: R4's heater raises temperature to trigger R2, and R2's open window/fan lowers temperature to re-trigger R4, with neither rule undoing the other's action.

conflicts.situation: Weekdays at 10:00, when the robot vacuum starts cleaning and moves through the living room, often while nobody is home.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The living-room motion sensor detects the vacuum, so the entrance door unlocks while the house may be empty. This is a security risk.
conflicts.explanation: R1 starts the vacuum. Its movement sets motion_living to True, which triggers R2, and R2 assumes the motion means a person is home.

conflicts.situation: Weekdays at 10:00, while home_mode is away and the vacuum cleans the living room.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: A false burglar alarm: the siren goes off with no intruder, which disturbs neighbours and can lead to unnecessary calls to security.
conflicts.explanation: The vacuum's movement sets motion_living to True. With the home in away mode, R3 treats this as an intruder and turns on the siren.

conflicts.situation: Weekdays at 10:00, when the vacuum's cleaning route goes through the bedroom.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The entrance light turns on for no reason, possibly while no one is home, which wastes energy.
conflicts.explanation: The vacuum's movement in the bedroom sets motion_bedroom to True, which triggers R4 to turn on the entrance light.

conflicts.situation: Smoke is detected in the kitchen (smoke_kitchen == True) while home_mode switches to away at about the same time or afterwards (e.g., residents leave, or presence/geofence sets away mode).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 relocks the apartment door that R1 unlocked for evacuation, so the door is locked during a fire and can trap people inside or block responders.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets lock_door.lock to unlocked and R2 sets it to locked. Neither rule has a condition that excludes the other, so both can fire together and the last one to fire decides the door state.

conflicts.situation: Smoke has been detected in the kitchen and is still present when the clock reaches 08:00 (e.g., a fire during breakfast cooking).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The air handler that R1 turned off is turned back on at 08:00. It then spreads smoke through the apartment and can feed the fire with air.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets hvac.power to off and R4 sets it to on. R4 has no condition that checks for smoke, so it overrides the safety shutdown.

conflicts.situation: Home is in night mode (R5 turns the aquarium heater off) and the aquarium water temperature is or falls below 24 C, firing R2.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The aquarium heater is switched off and on in opposition: either the fish are left with water that is too cold all night, or the heater runs at night and the goal of keeping the room quiet fails.
conflicts.explanation: R5 sets aquarium_heater.power := off on night mode, while R2 sets the same device to on when water_temp < 24. Turning the heater off makes the water cool down, so both rules can fire during the same night with opposite commands.

conflicts.situation: Home is in away mode (main valve closed by R1) and the clock reaches 06:00.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Irrigation is commanded on (watering and flow on) but receives no water; garden is not watered while the system believes it is, and pump/valves may run dry.
conflicts.explanation: The irrigation system depends on the main water supply. R1 closes the main valve, so R2's watering action cannot work.

conflicts.situation: A leak in the utility room has been detected (main valve closed by R3) and it is 06:00.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Irrigation starts against a closed supply, so watering fails silently and the system tries to draw water during a leak condition.
conflicts.explanation: R3 cuts the main water supply that R2's irrigation physically depends on, and R2 does not check the valve state.

conflicts.situation: Home is in away mode (outdoor tap valve closed by R5) and it is 06:00.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The garden irrigation fed from the outdoor tap gets no water while it is commanded on, so the garden goes unwatered while the owners are away.
conflicts.explanation: If irrigation is fed from the outdoor (garden) valve, which is likely but not stated, R5 closing it blocks the flow R2 tries to start.

conflicts.situation: Sunny daytime: lux_living rises above 800 and R1 closes the living room blinds.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Closing the blinds drops lux_living below 150, so R2 turns on the ceiling lights during the day. Daylight is replaced by electric light, which wastes energy, and no rule turns the lights off again.
conflicts.explanation: R1's action (blinds closed) cuts natural light in the room, which lowers lux_living and fires R2's dark trigger unexpectedly.

conflicts.situation: At 07:30 on a bright morning (e.g. summer or sun facing the window), when outdoor light makes lux_living exceed 800 as soon as the blinds open.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R3 opens the blinds and R1 closes them again right away. The blinds open and shut in quick succession, and the morning opening is cancelled for the whole day.
conflicts.explanation: R3 and R1 set opposite positions on blinds_living, and R3's action creates the condition that fires R1, so the two rules work against each other.

conflicts.situation: After 20:00 the nursery humidifier is running and nursery humidity climbs above 55 %.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The dehumidifier switches on and runs against the humidifier. Both appliances waste energy fighting each other, the baby doesn't get the intended humidity, and the loud dehumidifier runs in the nursery during sleep.
conflicts.explanation: R1 turns on the humidifier, which raises nursery humidity. That rise triggers R2, which starts the dehumidifier to cancel R1's effect.

conflicts.situation: At or after 20:00 nursery humidity is above 55 % (for example, because R1's humidifier pushed it up).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The dehumidifier is switched off at 20:00 for quiet sleep, then switched back on by the humidity trigger. It can also flip on and off around 20:00, so the nursery isn't quiet at night.
conflicts.explanation: R5 sets dehumidifier_nursery.power to off at 20:00. R2 sets the same device to on whenever humidity goes above 55 %, with no time restriction, so the two rules give opposite commands in the same evening period.

conflicts.situation: Night mode was activated in the evening (R1 cut the bedroom wall switch) and later the wake-up alarm rings (R2) while the switch is still off.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The bedroom bulb cannot turn on or fade to 60 % because it has no power, so the wake-up light fails.
conflicts.explanation: The bedroom bulb is powered through the bedroom wall switch. R1 turns the switch off and nothing turns it back on, so R2's commands to the bulb have no effect.

conflicts.situation: Someone arrives home between 17:00 and 19:00, around 18:00 when R1 fires
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Thermostat receives contradictory commands: 23 C heat vs 19 C eco; final state depends on execution order
conflicts.explanation: Both rules set thermostat setpoint and mode to incompatible values in overlapping time windows.

conflicts.situation: At 18:00 R1 heats to 23 C; on a warm evening or with overshoot the living room exceeds 24 C
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Heating and air-conditioner cooling run at the same time and fight each other, wasting energy
conflicts.explanation: R1's heating raises temp_living, which can trigger R3 to cool, while the thermostat remains in heat mode.

conflicts.situation: The living room fell below 20 C overnight (R4 set heat), then at 08:00 R5 fires while the room is still cold
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Thermostat switched to eco while the room is still cold; R4 is edge-triggered and doesn't re-fire, so the flat stays cold or the mode keeps switching
conflicts.explanation: Both rules write thermostat.mode with incompatible values (heat vs eco) under overlapping situations.

conflicts.situation: On arrival between 17:00 and 19:00, R2 sets 19 C eco; the room then cools below 20 C
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R4 switches the thermostat to heat, undoing the eco setting and causing the mode to flip between eco and heat
conflicts.explanation: R2's lower eco setpoint lets temp_living drop below 20 C, which triggers R4 to set heat mode.

conflicts.situation: Home is in away mode, so the garage breaker is off, and carbon monoxide is detected in the garage.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The exhaust fan and the garage door opener get no power, so the garage is not ventilated and CO builds up.
conflicts.explanation: R1 cuts power to the garage circuit, which the fan and door opener depend on. R2's safety actions fail without any warning.

conflicts.situation: CO is detected in the garage at about the same time the home switches to away mode, or while it is in away mode.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The garage door is told to open and to close at the same time. If it ends up closed, the CO is trapped.
conflicts.explanation: R2 sets garage_door.position to open and R3 sets it to closed, and both can fire together.

conflicts.situation: The home switches to away mode, which fires R1 and R3 together.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: If the breaker turns off before the door closes, the garage door stays open while the occupants are away. This is a security risk.
conflicts.explanation: The garage door opener is likely on the garage circuit that R1 switches off, so R3's close command may not run.

conflicts.situation: The car is parked and charging in the garage when the home switches to away mode.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: EV charging stops, so the car may not be charged when it is needed.
conflicts.explanation: The EV charger is powered by the garage circuit, and R1 cuts that circuit, which overrides R4's charging.

conflicts.situation: Motion is detected in the kitchen while home_mode == home
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The kitchen camera gets both 'recording on' (R3) and 'recording off' (R6) at the same moment, so whether it records depends on which rule runs last. The privacy setting may not be applied, or recording may stop when it shouldn't.
conflicts.explanation: R3 has no condition and fires on every kitchen motion event, including in home mode, where R6 fires on the same trigger. The two rules set the same camera state to opposite values.

conflicts.situation: A fall is detected (R3 unlocks the entrance door), and then, before paramedics arrive, the home switches to night mode (R4 locks the entrance door).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The entrance door is locked again during a medical emergency, so paramedics cannot get in.
conflicts.explanation: R3 and R4 set opposite states on the same lock (unlocked vs. locked). Neither rule has a condition that excludes the other, so whichever fires last wins, and night mode can override the emergency unlock.

conflicts.situation: On a warm day the living room is above 27 C, so R1 has the AC cooling and R6 has closed the window. Then at 10:00 R2 opens it. Or R2 opens it first and R6 later closes it when the AC starts.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The living room window opens while the AC is cooling (energy waste, poor cooling), or the fresh-air airing gets cut short. The window ends up in contradictory states.
conflicts.explanation: R2 sets window_living to open and R6 sets it to closed, and both can apply during the same warm morning. R6 only fires when the AC starts cooling, so it won't close the window again after R2 opens it while the AC is already running.

conflicts.situation: Home switches to night mode before 01:00; at 01:00 R1 tries to start the NAS backup while the closet power strip (which feeds the NAS in the closet) is off.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The nightly NAS backup fails or never runs because the NAS has no power.
conflicts.explanation: R2 cuts power to the closet power strip, which the NAS presumably plugs into. R1's backup action depends on that power, but the rule doesn't say so.

conflicts.situation: Night mode is active (closet strip off) and the closet temperature rises above 35 C, e.g. during heavy equipment load.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The cooling fan can't turn on, so the closet overheats and equipment may be damaged.
conflicts.explanation: The closet fan is likely powered from the closet power strip that R2 turned off, so R3's 'fan on' command has no effect.

conflicts.situation: Teenager's phone arrives home between 23:00 and 06:00
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Front door is unlocked by R1 and immediately relocked by R2; teenager may be locked out and the lock may oscillate
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets lock_front to unlocked, which directly triggers R2 during the night window to set it locked again, issuing contradictory commands on the same lock.

conflicts.situation: Every day at 09:00, when both rules trigger at the same time with no conditions
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The office shades get two opposite commands (closed and open) at once. Their final position depends on which command runs last, so the shades may flap or stay in the wrong position for screen work or daylight use.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules have the same time trigger and no conditions, and they set shades_office.position to opposite values.

conflicts.situation: At 19:30 R2 starts the nursery white-noise speaker; its output raises the measured nursery sound level above 60 dB.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 mistakes the white noise for the baby crying and turns on the nursery lamp at bedtime, possibly waking the baby or leaving the lamp on all evening.
conflicts.explanation: R2's action directly raises noise_nursery, the variable R1 uses to detect crying, so R1 fires without the baby actually crying.

conflicts.situation: A frost warning is active in the evening or at night, and the clock reaches 22:00.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The greenhouse heater turns off during the frost, and plants may freeze.
conflicts.explanation: R1 turns the heater on because of the frost warning. At 22:00, R6 turns it off no matter what the weather is, and R1 won't fire again unless a new warning is issued.

conflicts.situation: A frost warning is active, and R1's heater raises the greenhouse above 18 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The roof vent opens during a frost and lets freezing air in. Heat is wasted and the temperature swings.
conflicts.explanation: The heater turned on by R1 raises temp_gh past 18 C, which sets off R2 and opens the vent while it is freezing outside. The vent only closes again once the greenhouse is below 5 C (R5).

conflicts.situation: Night mode is on and hallway motion is detected between 22:00 and 06:00.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R4 unlocks the front door that R3 locked, so the apartment stays unlocked overnight.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules act on lock_front.lock with opposite values (locked vs unlocked), and their triggers overlap at night.

conflicts.situation: At 23:00 while the home is in away mode, assuming the hallway camera (or its hub) is powered through the hallway smart plug.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The hallway camera loses power and stops recording while the occupants are away.
conflicts.explanation: R1 cuts power to plug_hall, and the hallway camera that R2 relies on for recording likely depends on that plug. This dependency is not stated in either rule.

conflicts.situation: At 18:00 while the home is in away mode
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The living room heater is told to turn on and off at the same moment, so its final state depends on which rule runs last.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules fire at 18:00, and R5's condition (away mode) doesn't rule out R1, which has no condition. They send opposite commands to heater_living.power.

conflicts.situation: After 18:00, when the heater R1 turned on pushes the living room above 26 C
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The fan runs and the window opens while the heater keeps heating, which wastes energy and makes the systems fight each other.
conflicts.explanation: R1 turns the heater on and nothing turns it off. The heat triggers R2, which ventilates and opens the window but leaves the heater running.

conflicts.situation: The window is open after R2 fired (temperature was above 26 C), then cold outside air pulls the living room below 19 C
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The heater runs with the window open and the fan on, wasting energy. The heating and cooling can keep undoing each other.
conflicts.explanation: Opening the window (R2) lowers the room temperature, which triggers R4 to turn on the heater. Neither rule closes the window or turns the heater off, so both keep acting at the same time.

conflicts.situation: Weekdays at 10:00 the robot vacuum starts cleaning and moves through the living room, typically while occupants are out.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The entrance door is unlocked while nobody is home, creating a security breach.
conflicts.explanation: The vacuum's movement is detected by the living-room motion sensor, setting motion_living to True, which triggers R2 to unlock the entrance door as if a person were home.

conflicts.situation: Weekdays at 10:00 while home_mode is away, the robot vacuum cleans the living room.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: False intrusion alarm: the siren sounds with no intruder present.
conflicts.explanation: The vacuum triggers the living-room motion sensor; with the home in away mode, R3 interprets this as an intrusion and activates the siren.

conflicts.situation: Smoke is detected in the kitchen while the home mode switches to away (or away mode is set during/after the smoke event).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The apartment door is re-locked during a fire, blocking evacuation or emergency access.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets lock_door to unlocked for evacuation while R2 sets the same lock to locked on away mode; neither rule checks the other's context, so the last-firing action wins.

conflicts.situation: Smoke is detected in the kitchen shortly before or at 08:00.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The air handler is switched back on during a fire, spreading smoke through the apartment.
conflicts.explanation: R1 turns hvac off when smoke is detected, but R4's unconditional 08:00 timer turns hvac on regardless of the ongoing smoke condition.

conflicts.situation: Home switches to night mode while aquarium water temperature is below 24 C, or water cools below 24 C during the night after R5 switched the heater off.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Aquarium heater is switched off and back on; the heater either runs at night (defeating the quiet goal) or stays off and the water gets too cold for the fish, with possible on/off oscillation.
conflicts.explanation: R5 sets aquarium_heater.power to off on night mode while R2 sets it to on when water_temp < 24; both can be active simultaneously, and R5's action itself lets the water cool until R2 fires.

conflicts.situation: The home is in away mode (main water valve closed by R1) and it is 06:00, when R2 starts watering.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Irrigation is switched on but gets no water, so the garden is not watered while the occupants are away. The irrigation pump or flow may also run dry.
conflicts.explanation: The irrigation system depends on the main water supply. R1 cuts that supply, and nothing in R2 accounts for it, so R2's watering action silently fails.

conflicts.situation: A leak in the utility room has triggered R3, which closed the main valve. At 06:00, R2 turns irrigation and flow on.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Watering is commanded with no water supply, so the garden goes unwatered and the irrigation equipment may run dry until someone reopens the valve.
conflicts.explanation: R3 closes the main valve that feeds the irrigation system. R2 does not check the valve state, so its action has no effect.

conflicts.situation: The home is in away mode, so R5 has closed the outdoor/garden tap valve. At 06:00, R2 starts irrigation.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The garden irrigation fed by the outdoor tap gets no water, so plants are not watered during the absence even though the schedule shows watering as on.
conflicts.explanation: The irrigation system depends on the garden valve, which R5 closes. R2 still turns watering on, so the command reports watering as on but no water flows.

conflicts.situation: Bright daytime: living room light goes above 800 lux, so R1 closes the blinds.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: With the blinds shut, the room can drop below 150 lux. R2 then turns on the ceiling lights in the middle of a sunny day, which wastes energy and works against the reason for closing the blinds.
conflicts.explanation: R1 closes the blinds, which blocks daylight and lowers lux_living. That lower reading meets R2's trigger, so R2 fires even though there is plenty of light outside.

conflicts.situation: At 07:30 on a bright morning, R3 opens the blinds and sunlight pushes the living room above 800 lux.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 closes the blinds again right after R3 opens them. The scheduled morning opening is cancelled, and the blinds can keep moving back and forth.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules control blinds_living.position and set opposite values (open vs. closed). They can both fire at the same moment, because R3's action is what triggers R1.

conflicts.situation: From 20:00 the nursery humidifier runs and pushes nursery humidity above 55 %.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The dehumidifier switches on and the two devices run against each other all night. This wastes energy, and the room never holds the humidity intended for the baby's sleep.
conflicts.explanation: R1's humidifier raises humidity_nursery, which crosses R2's 55 % threshold and turns on the dehumidifier. The dehumidifier then cancels out the humidifier's effect.

conflicts.situation: At night after 20:00, nursery humidity is above 55 % (for example because the humidifier from R1 is running).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The loud dehumidifier turns back on while the baby is sleeping, which defeats R5's 20:00 shut-off.
conflicts.explanation: R5 turns dehumidifier_nursery off at 20:00. R2 has no time condition, so it turns the dehumidifier back on whenever humidity goes above 55 %, and both rules can fire on the same evening.

conflicts.situation: Home is in night mode (bedroom wall switch turned off by R1) and the wake-up alarm rings in the morning, triggering R2.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The bedroom bulb gets no power, so it does not turn on or fade to 60 %. The wake-up light fails.
conflicts.explanation: The bedroom bulb is most likely powered through the bedroom wall switch. R1 cuts that power and nothing turns it back on before the alarm, so R2's command to the bulb has no effect.

conflicts.situation: Someone arrives home between 17:00 and 19:00. R1 fires at 18:00 and R2 fires on arrival in the same window.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The thermostat switches between 23 °C heat and 19 °C eco. The final state depends on arrival order, so the home is too cold or too warm.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules set incompatible setpoint and mode values on the same thermostat, and both can fire in the 17:00-19:00 window.

conflicts.situation: The living room is below 20 °C and someone arrives between 17:00 and 19:00.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2's eco mode at 19 °C cancels R4's heat mode, so the cold room is not heated.
conflicts.explanation: R4 sets thermostat.mode to heat and R2 sets it to eco. Both can be active in the same evening situation, and eco at 19 °C keeps the room below R4's 20 °C threshold.

conflicts.situation: Around 08:00, when the living room is below 20 °C or drops below it after 08:00.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The thermostat mode goes back and forth between eco and heat. Either heating is cut while the room is cold, or the eco schedule is overridden.
conflicts.explanation: R5 sets thermostat.mode to eco at 08:00 and R4 sets it to heat when the room is below 20 °C. These are incompatible states on the same device.

conflicts.situation: Home is in away mode (garage breaker switched off) and carbon monoxide is detected in the garage.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Exhaust fan and garage door opener have no power, so CO is not vented and accumulates/spreads into the house.
conflicts.explanation: R1 cuts power to the garage circuit, which feeds the fan and door opener that R2 relies on for its safety response.

conflicts.situation: Home switches to away mode while CO is present in the garage (e.g., car running as occupants leave).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Garage door is commanded both open and closed; if closed, CO is trapped in the garage.
conflicts.explanation: R2 sets garage_door to open and R3 sets it to closed; both can fire simultaneously, giving an incompatible/racing door state.

conflicts.situation: Car is parked in the garage and charging, then home switches to away mode.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: EV charging is interrupted and the car is left uncharged.
conflicts.explanation: The EV charger is powered by the garage circuit that R1 switches off, undoing R4's charging action.

conflicts.situation: Motion detected in the kitchen while home_mode == home
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Kitchen camera receives both recording on and recording off; it may record occupants against privacy intent or toggle unpredictably
conflicts.explanation: R3 has no condition and turns recording on for every kitchen motion, while R6 turns it off for the same trigger in home mode, so both fire together with contradictory actions.

conflicts.situation: 12:00 while home_mode == away and the feeder is in the kitchen
conflicts.undesired_outcome: False siren alarm while the occupants are away
conflicts.explanation: Dispensing food draws the cat to the kitchen, its motion sets motion_kitchen to True, and R2 sounds the alarm because the home is in away mode.

conflicts.situation: A fall is detected in the evening and the door is unlocked for paramedics. Then the home switches to night mode before help arrives (or both events happen at about the same time).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R4 locks the entrance door again, so paramedics may be locked out of the home during a medical emergency.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules set lock_entrance.lock, one to unlocked and the other to locked. No condition keeps R4 from overriding R3's emergency unlock.

conflicts.situation: Warm day with living room above 27 C: at 10:00 R2 opens the living room window while the AC is cooling or starts cooling (via R1), firing R6.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: window_living receives contradictory open/closed commands; either fresh-air opening is immediately undone, or (if AC was already cooling before 10:00, so R6 does not re-fire) the window stays open while the AC cools, wasting energy.
conflicts.explanation: R2 sets window_living to open at a fixed time regardless of AC state, while R6 sets the same window to closed whenever the AC enters cool mode. Both can apply in the same period, giving incompatible actions on the same device.

conflicts.situation: Home switches to night mode before 01:00; the closet power strip (which supplies the NAS located in the closet) is turned off, then at 01:00 R1 starts the backup.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The nightly NAS backup fails or never runs because the NAS has lost power; an in-progress backup could also be interrupted, risking data corruption.
conflicts.explanation: R2 cuts power to the closet strip, which the NAS implicitly depends on, while R1 expects the NAS to be powered to run the backup.

conflicts.situation: In night mode (closet strip off), the closet temperature exceeds 35 C, e.g. due to the NAS backup heat.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R3 commands the cooling fan on but the fan is unpowered, so the closet overheats, risking equipment damage.
conflicts.explanation: The closet fan is plausibly powered via the closet power strip; R2 cutting the strip silently defeats R3's cooling action.

conflicts.situation: The teenager's phone arrives home between 23:00 and 06:00.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 unlocks the front door and R2 locks it again right away. The teenager can be locked out, or the lock flips between locked and unlocked and its final state is unclear.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules set lock_front.lock to opposite values. R1 has no time condition, so it can fire during R2's 23:00–06:00 window, and R1's unlock is exactly what triggers R2.

conflicts.situation: Every day at 09:00, when both rules fire at the same time
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The office shades are told to close and to open at the same moment. Their final position depends on which command runs last, so screen glare or loss of daylight is unpredictable.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules have the same time trigger and no conditions, and they set shades_office.position to opposite values (closed vs. open).

conflicts.situation: From 19:30 the white-noise speaker plays in the nursery while the baby is asleep, and its output pushes the measured nursery sound level above 60 dB.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 takes the white noise for a crying baby and turns on the nursery lamp, so the room gets light at bedtime and the baby may wake up.
conflicts.explanation: R2 raises the nursery sound level, which is the same variable R1 uses to detect crying. The noise sensor can't tell the speaker's white noise from crying, so R1 fires when it shouldn't.

conflicts.situation: A frost warning is active (or is issued) in the evening, and the time reaches 22:00 while frost_warning == True.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R6 turns the greenhouse heater off at 22:00 even though R1 turned it on because of the frost warning. The greenhouse is left unheated through the coldest part of the night, and plants may be damaged by frost.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets gh_heater.power to on and R6 sets the same device to off. Neither rule has a condition that rules out the other, so the fixed 22:00 shutdown overrides the frost protection whenever a frost warning is active at night.

conflicts.situation: At night (22:00–06:00) the home is in night mode and R3 has locked the front door, then someone moves in the hallway.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R4 unlocks the front door that R3 just locked, so the apartment stays unlocked overnight. R4 can also fire before or after R3, so the lock keeps switching between locked and unlocked.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules set lock_front.lock to opposite values, and their situations overlap: night mode and hallway motion between 22:00 and 06:00 can both happen at the same time.

conflicts.situation: The home is in away mode and R2 has started recording on the hallway camera. At 23:00, R1 turns off the hallway smart plug, which likely powers the hallway camera.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The hallway camera loses power and stops recording while nobody is home, so there is no security footage overnight.
conflicts.explanation: R1 cuts power to the hallway plug at a fixed time without checking the home mode. If the camera runs off that plug, which the rules don't say but is plausible, turning the plug off overrides R2's recording.

conflicts.situation: At 18:00 when the home is in away mode
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The living room heater gets both an on and an off command at the same moment. Its final state depends on which rule runs last, so it may heat an empty house.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules trigger at 18:00 and act on heater_living.power. R1 has no condition, so in away mode it sets the heater on while R5 sets it off.

conflicts.situation: Evening after 18:00, when the heater R1 turned on pushes the living room temperature above 26 C
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The fan runs and the window opens while the heater stays on. Heat escapes outside and energy is wasted.
conflicts.explanation: R1's heating raises temp_living, which triggers R2. No rule turns the heater off, so heating and venting run at the same time.

conflicts.situation: After R2 has opened the window and turned on the fan, the living room cools below 19 C (for example, on a cold evening)
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The heater runs while the window is still open and the fan is on. This wastes energy and can make the system swing between heating and venting.
conflicts.explanation: R2's open window and fan lower temp_living, which triggers R4 to turn the heater on. Nothing closes the window, so the heater warms the room until R2 fires again.

conflicts.situation: Weekday 10:00, residents typically away; the robot vacuum starts cleaning and moves through the living room, so motion_living becomes True.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The entrance door is unlocked while nobody is home, which is a security breach.
conflicts.explanation: The vacuum's movement is picked up by the living-room motion sensor. R2 reads that motion as a person being home and unlocks the entrance door.

conflicts.situation: Weekday 10:00 with home_mode == away; the vacuum cleans the living room and triggers motion_living.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: False alarm: the siren sounds with no intruder, disturbing neighbours and possibly causing an unneeded security response.
conflicts.explanation: R1's cleaning action creates motion in the living room. R3 treats any living-room motion in away mode as an intrusion and turns on the siren.

conflicts.situation: The vacuum started at 10:00 by R1 enters the bedroom and triggers motion_bedroom.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The entrance light is turned on in the daytime with nobody present, wasting energy.
conflicts.explanation: The vacuum's movement sets off the bedroom motion sensor, which unexpectedly fires R4.

conflicts.situation: Smoke is detected in the kitchen while the home is in away mode, or the home switches to away mode during or after a smoke event (for example, someone is still inside or pets are home).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The apartment door gets locked again after R1 unlocked it for evacuation, or it stays locked. This blocks the evacuation route and keeps responders out.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets lock_door.lock to unlocked and R2 sets it to locked. Neither rule checks the other's situation, so whichever fires last decides the door's state, even during a fire.

conflicts.situation: Smoke is detected in the kitchen shortly before or at 08:00, and smoke is still present when the 08:00 schedule fires.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The air handler turns back on during a smoke event. It can spread smoke through the apartment and feed the fire air, undoing R1's safety shutdown.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets hvac.power to off when smoke is detected. R4 sets hvac.power to on at 08:00 with no check for smoke, so it overrides the emergency shutdown.

conflicts.situation: The home is in night mode and the aquarium water temperature is below 24 C, or drops below 24 C during the night.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The aquarium heater flips between on and off. Either R5 turns it off while the water is already too cold, which puts the fish at risk, or R2 turns it back on and undoes the night-time quiet setting.
conflicts.explanation: R5 turns the heater off when night mode starts. R2 turns it on whenever the water is below 24 C. Both can apply at night with nothing to decide which one wins, so the heater state depends on which rule fires last.

conflicts.situation: Home is in away mode (main water valve closed by R1) when the 06:00 daily irrigation start (R2) fires.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Irrigation is switched on (watering and flow on) but gets no water: the garden isn't watered, the pump or controller may run dry, and soil moisture never goes above 60 %, so R4 never stops the watering.
conflicts.explanation: The irrigation system gets its water through the main valve. R1 closes that valve, so R2's watering command can't work, even though neither rule mentions this dependency.

conflicts.situation: Home is in away mode (outdoor tap valve closed by R5) when R2 starts the garden watering at 06:00.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Garden irrigation is on but the outdoor tap valve is closed, so no water reaches the garden. The system keeps running with no flow, and R4's soil-moisture stop never fires.
conflicts.explanation: The garden irrigation is fed through the outdoor tap valve. R5 closing that valve physically blocks the watering that R2 starts.

conflicts.situation: Daytime with strong sunlight: lux_living rises above 800, R1 closes the living room blinds.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: With the blinds closed the room drops below 150 lux, R2 turns on the ceiling lights — daylight is blocked while electric lights burn, wasting energy.
conflicts.explanation: R1's action (closing blinds) reduces the living room light level, which creates the trigger condition for R2 (lux_living < 150).

conflicts.situation: Sunny morning at 07:30: R3 opens the living room blinds and lux_living immediately exceeds 800.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 closes the blinds right after R3 opened them, so the scheduled morning opening is undone and the blinds stay closed; possible open/close toggling of the same device.
conflicts.explanation: R3 sets blinds_living.position to open while R1 sets it to closed; R3's own effect (letting in light) satisfies R1's trigger, so both fire on the same device in contradictory ways.

conflicts.situation: From 20:00, when the nursery humidifier raises humidity above 55 %
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Dehumidifier turns on and fights the humidifier: energy waste, unstable humidity and noise during the baby's sleep
conflicts.explanation: R1's humidifier raises nursery humidity, which triggers R2 to turn on the dehumidifier and undo R1's purpose.

conflicts.situation: After 20:00, when nursery humidity rises above 55 % (e.g. due to the humidifier)
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The dehumidifier that R5 switched off for quiet sleep is turned back on by R2 and disturbs the baby
conflicts.explanation: R5 sets dehumidifier_nursery off at 20:00 while R2 sets it on when humidity > 55 %; both can apply during the night, giving opposite commands to the same device.

conflicts.situation: The home switches to night mode in the evening, and the wake-up alarm rings the next morning while the bedroom wall switch is still off.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The bedroom bulb doesn't turn on or fade in to 60% when the alarm rings, so the wake-up light fails silently.
conflicts.explanation: R1 turns off the bedroom wall switch, which most likely powers the bedroom bulb. R2 then sends power-on and brightness commands to a bulb that has no power, so they have no effect.

conflicts.situation: Someone arrives home between 17:00 and 19:00, so R2 fires close to the 18:00 R1 trigger. For example, R2 fires at 17:45 and R1 fires at 18:00, or R1 fires first and then someone arrives at 18:30.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The thermostat gets setpoint 23 C in heat mode and setpoint 19 C in eco mode. Whichever rule fires last wins, so the result depends on timing: either the comfort heating is undone or the eco saving is lost.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules write different values to thermostat.setpoint and thermostat.mode, and their time windows overlap (18:00 falls within 17:00–19:00).

conflicts.situation: Someone arrives between 17:00 and 19:00 while the living room is below 20 C, or the 19 C eco setpoint lets the room cool below 20 C after arrival.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The thermostat mode switches between eco (R2) and heat (R4), so the eco setting the user asked for on arrival is overridden.
conflicts.explanation: R2 sets thermostat.mode to eco with a 19 C setpoint, which keeps the room near or below 20 C. That is exactly the condition that makes R4 set thermostat.mode to heat.

conflicts.situation: At 08:00 the living room is below 20 C (for example on a cold morning), or it falls below 20 C after eco mode starts.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R5 sets eco mode, but R4 then switches the thermostat back to heat (or the other way round), so the morning eco schedule doesn't hold and energy is wasted.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules set thermostat.mode to different values, eco and heat. R5's eco mode lowers the heating, which makes it more likely that the room drops below 20 C and R4 fires.

conflicts.situation: Home is in away mode (garage breaker off) and carbon monoxide is detected in the garage.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Exhaust fan and garage door opener have no power, so CO cannot be vented and accumulates.
conflicts.explanation: R1 cuts the garage circuit, which powers the fan and door motor that R2 relies on; this dependency is not stated in the rules.

conflicts.situation: Car is parked in the garage while the home is in away mode with the garage breaker switched off.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: EV charging fails or is interrupted; the car is not charged.
conflicts.explanation: The EV charger is supplied by the garage circuit that R1 switches off, so R4's charging command has no effect.

conflicts.situation: CO is detected in the garage around the time the home switches to away mode.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Garage door receives open and close commands; if closed, CO is trapped inside the garage.
conflicts.explanation: R2 sets garage_door to open while R3 sets it to closed; both can fire together, and the last command wins, possibly overriding the safety ventilation.

conflicts.situation: Motion is detected in the kitchen while home_mode == home.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The kitchen camera receives both recording := on (R3) and recording := off (R6) at the same time, so the result is nondeterministic and may break privacy or the intended behavior.
conflicts.explanation: R3 has no mode condition, so it fires in home mode too, at the same time as R6. The two rules send opposite commands to the same camera state.

conflicts.situation: At 12:00 while home_mode == away, the feeder dispenses food and the cat comes into the kitchen to eat (assuming the feeder is in the kitchen).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The cat's movement triggers the kitchen motion sensor and the siren sounds as a false intruder alarm every day at noon while the occupants are away.
conflicts.explanation: R1 creates motion in the kitchen through the cat. R2 reads kitchen motion in away mode as an intrusion and turns the siren on.

conflicts.situation: A fall is detected (R3 unlocks the entrance door for paramedics) and the home mode then switches to night mode (or both happen around the same time) while help is still on the way.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R4 locks the entrance door again, so paramedics cannot get in to reach the person who fell. In the reverse order, the door is left unlocked at night.
conflicts.explanation: R3 and R4 set lock_entrance to opposite states (unlocked vs. locked). Neither rule has a condition that excludes the other, so both can fire in the same period.

conflicts.situation: At 10:00 while the living room AC is already in cool mode (or AC starts cooling later in the morning).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R2 opens the living room window while the AC is cooling; R6 only fires on the transition to cool, so the window stays open during cooling (energy waste), or R6 closes it and cancels R2's ventilation.
conflicts.explanation: R2 sets window_living to open and R6 sets it to closed; both can be active at the same time, giving contradictory window states.

conflicts.situation: Hot day, window opened at 10:00 while outdoor air is warmer than 27 C.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: Warm outside air raises the living room temperature above 27 C, so the AC starts cooling while the window is open. This wastes energy and the two rules work against each other.
conflicts.explanation: R2's window opening changes the indoor temperature, which unexpectedly triggers R1's cooling.

conflicts.situation: Night mode is active (it usually starts before 01:00), so the closet power strip is off when the backup is due at 01:00.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The nightly NAS backup can't run, or it is cut off partway through, which can corrupt the backup or the NAS.
conflicts.explanation: The NAS is probably plugged into the closet power strip. R2 turns the strip off in night mode, which also cuts power to the NAS that R1 needs for its backup.

conflicts.situation: Night mode is active and the closet strip is off, but the closet temperature goes above 35 °C (for example, because equipment is still running or the night is hot).
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R3 turns the cooling fan on, but the fan gets no power, so the closet overheats.
conflicts.explanation: The closet cooling fan probably gets its power from the closet power strip. R2 turns that strip off, so R3's command to turn on the fan has no effect.

conflicts.situation: The teenager's phone arrives home between 23:00 and 06:00.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: R1 unlocks the front door for the teenager, which immediately triggers R2 to lock it again. The teenager is locked out, or the lock flips back and forth.
conflicts.explanation: Both rules act on lock_front.lock and set opposite values. During the night window, R1's unlock is exactly the trigger for R2, so the two rules work against each other.

conflicts.situation: Every day at 09:00; both rules are triggered by the same time event and have no conditions.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The office shades are commanded closed and open at the same moment; the final position is nondeterministic and either screen work or daylight use is defeated.
conflicts.explanation: R1 sets shades_office.position to closed and R6 sets it to open on the identical trigger, issuing incompatible commands to the same device state.

conflicts.situation: At 19:30 R2 starts the nursery white-noise speaker; white noise played at typical levels (about 50-65 dB) can push noise_nursery above 60 dB while the baby is calm.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: The nursery lamp turns on at bedtime with no real reason and can keep the baby awake or wake them. Crying detection also stops being useful while the white noise keeps the sound level high.
conflicts.explanation: The white-noise speaker raises the nursery sound level that R1 uses to detect crying, so R1 fires because of R2's action instead of a crying baby.

conflicts.situation: A frost warning is active (frost_warning == True) in the evening. R1 has turned the greenhouse heater on, and then the clock reaches 22:00.
conflicts.undesired_outcome: At 22:00, R6 turns the greenhouse heater off even though the frost warning is still active. The greenhouse stays unheated for the coldest part of the night, and the plants can be damaged by frost.
